words.en: If you describe a good event as miraculous, you mean that it is very surprising and unexpected.

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.ex: The pirate sailed the sea with a black flag.
words.ex_cn: 海盗带着黑旗在海上航行。
words.en: A pirate is someone who attacks and robs ships at sea. The term can also refer to someone who illegally copies and distributes software, music, or films.

words.ex: He finally conceded defeat after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于承认失败了。
words.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct.

words.ex: They tease him because he wears funny hats.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他戴滑稽的帽子而戏弄他。
words.en: To tease someone means to make fun of them or try to provoke them in a playful way.

words.tr:
v. 疏浚；挖掘
n. 挖泥船；疏浚机
words.ex: They dredge the river to remove mud.
words.ex_cn: 他们疏浚河流以清除淤泥。
words.en: To dredge means to remove mud, sand, or other material from the bottom of a river, lake, etc., in order to make it deeper or to search for something.

words.tr: n. 织物；（建筑物的）结构；
words.ex: The dress is made of soft fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子是由柔软的织物制成的。
words.en: Fabric refers to cloth or other material produced by weaving together cotton, nylon, wool, silk, or other threads. It can also refer to the basic structure of a building or a system.

words.ex: The consumption of water has increased this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年水的消耗量增加了。
words.en: Consumption is the act of buying and using products.

words.ex: He gave a heartless reply to her plea.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的恳求给出了无情的答复。
words.en: If you describe someone as heartless, you mean that they are cruel and unkind, and have no sympathy for anyone or anything.

words.ex: The Earth revolves around the Sun.
words.ex_cn: 地球围绕太阳转。
words.en: If something revolves or if you revolve something, it moves or turns around a central point or line.

words.ex: He studied hard, thereby passing the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习，因此通过了考试。
words.en: You use thereby to introduce an important result or consequence of the event or action you have just mentioned.

words.ex: The magic trick astounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们惊呆了。
words.en: If something astounds you, it surprises or shocks you very much.

words.ex: The computer will execute the program quickly.
words.ex_cn: 计算机将快速执行该程序。
words.en: To execute means to carry out or put into effect a plan, order, or course of action. It can also refer to the act of legally killing someone as a punishment.

words.ex: The injury impaired his ability to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤损害了他走路的能力。
words.en: If something impairs something such as an ability or the way something works, it damages it or makes it worse.

words.ex: The volcano spewed hot magma into the air.
words.ex_cn: 火山喷出了炽热的岩浆。
words.en: Magma is molten rock that is found beneath the surface of the Earth, and which may erupt from a volcano as lava.

words.tr:
v. （使）旋转
n. 转环；旋轴
words.ex: The chair can swivel easily.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子可以轻松旋转。
words.en: A swivel is a device that allows something to turn around freely, or to turn something around freely.

words.ex: The city had an economic boom after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市迎来了经济繁荣。
words.en: If there is a boom in the economy, there is an increase in economic activity, for example in the amount of things that are being bought and sold.

words.tr: adj. 没有希望的；无前途的；不乐观的
words.ex: The weather looks unpromising for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气看起来不适合野餐。
words.en: If you describe something as unpromising, you think that it is unlikely to be successful or produce anything good in the future.

words.ex: He acquired a new skill last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了一项新技能。
words.en: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.

words.tr:
n. 绝望；
v. 绝望；
words.ex: He felt despair after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到绝望。
words.en: Despair is the feeling that everything is wrong and that nothing will improve.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.ex: He hurled the ball across the field.
words.ex_cn: 他猛地把球投过球场。
words.en: To throw something with great force; to shout something loudly.

words.tr: n. 精心制作；详尽的细节；
words.ex: The chef gave an elaboration to the dish with fresh herbs.
words.ex_cn: 厨师用新鲜香草对这道菜进行了精心制作。
words.en: The process of developing or presenting a theory, policy, or system in detail.

words.ex: The thermal blanket keeps you warm.
words.ex_cn: 这个保暖毯让你暖和。
words.en: relating to heat or temperature

words.tr: v. 接着发生；因而产生
words.ex: The storm ended, and peace ensued.
words.ex_cn: 风暴结束后，和平随之而来。
words.en: If something ensues, it happens immediately after another event, usually as a result of it.

words.tr:
v. 奔驰；飞奔
n. 奔驰；飞奔
words.ex: The horse gallops across the field.
words.ex_cn: 马在田野上疾驰。
words.en: If a horse gallops, it runs very fast so that all four legs are off the ground at the same time in each stride.

words.tr: adj. 富有成效的；多产的；生产的；
words.ex: He had a productive day and finished all his work.
words.ex_cn: 他度过了富有成效的一天，完成了所有工作。
words.en: Producing or able to produce large amounts of goods, crops, or other commodities.

words.tr: n. 低迷时期；衰退；下滑；
words.ex: Many businesses struggled during the economic downturn.
words.ex_cn: 许多企业在经济低迷时期挣扎求生。
words.en: A downturn is a period of time in which something such as business activity, production, or investment decreases or becomes worse.

words.ex: He had to endure the cold winter without a coat.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不在没有外套的情况下忍受寒冷的冬天。
words.en: To endure means to suffer something difficult, unpleasant, or painful, or to continue to exist for a long time.

words.ex: The old bridge began disintegration after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥在风暴后开始崩解。
words.en: The process of breaking into small parts or pieces and losing strength or effectiveness.

words.ex: This plant produces electricity using nuclear power.
words.ex_cn: 这座电厂使用核能发电。
words.en: relating to the nucleus of an atom, or to the energy produced when the nucleus of an atom is split or joined with another nucleus

words.tr:
n. 赞助商；
v. 赞助；
words.ex: The company is a sponsor of the football match.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是这场足球赛的赞助商。
words.en: A sponsor is a person or organization that pays for or contributes to the costs involved in staging a sporting or artistic event in return for advertising. A sponsor can also be someone who introduces and supports a proposal for a new law.

words.ex: Milk has a lot of calcium.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶含有大量的钙。
words.en: A chemical element that is present in teeth and bones and is necessary for their health.

words.ex: The interplay between light and shadow creates beauty.
words.ex_cn: 光与影的相互作用创造了美。
words.en: The way in which two or more things have an effect on each other.

words.ex: The tide comes in every twelve hours.
words.ex_cn: 潮汐每十二小时涨一次。
words.en: The tide is the regular change in the level of the sea on the shore.

words.ex: The precipitation increased last week.
words.ex_cn: 上周降水增加了。
words.en: Precipitation is rain, snow, sleet, or hail — any kind of weather condition where something's falling from the sky.

words.ex: He had an accidental fall while walking.
words.ex_cn: 他在走路时不小心摔了一跤。
words.en: An accidental event happens by chance, without being planned.

words.tr: adv. 无限期地；不确定地；
words.ex: The meeting was postponed indefinitely.
words.ex_cn: 会议被无限期推迟了。
words.en: If something will happen indefinitely, it will happen for an unlimited or unknown period of time.

words.ex: He can deduce the answer from the clues.
words.ex_cn: 他能从线索中推断出答案。
words.en: If you deduce something or deduce that something is true, you reach that conclusion because of other things that you know to be true.

words.ex: I am awaiting the bus.
words.ex_cn: 我正在等公交车。
words.en: If you await someone or something, you wait for them.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；茂盛的；
words.ex: He is a vigorous man who runs every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的人，每天早上都跑步。
words.en: A vigorous person does things with great energy and enthusiasm. A vigorous campaign or activity is done with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.ex: The glacier moves slowly down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 冰川缓慢地沿着山向下移动。
words.en: A glacier is a large, persistent body of ice that forms where the accumulation of snow exceeds its ablation over many years, often centuries.

words.ex: The village is at an altitude of 2,000 meters.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄的海拔是2000米。
words.en: The height of an object or point in relation to sea level or ground level.

words.tr:
n. 收获；收成；
v. 收获；收割；
words.ex: The farmers celebrated the harvest in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 农民们在秋天庆祝收获。
words.en: The harvest is the process of gathering mature crops from the fields. It is a crucial activity in agriculture that marks the end of the growing season.

words.tr: n. 举办地点；（比赛）地点；会场；
words.ex: The concert will be held at a new venue.
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会将在一个新的举办地点举行。
words.en: A place where an event or meeting is held, such as a concert hall or conference center.

words.ex: He used a stick to dislodge the rock from the path.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子把石头从路上移出。
words.en: To dislodge something means to remove it from a place where it is fixed or held.

words.ex: The equator divides the Earth into two halves.
words.ex_cn: 赤道将地球分为两半。
words.en: The equator is an imaginary line around the Earth, equally distant from the North Pole and the South Pole, dividing the Earth into the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere.

words.ex: He is undoubtedly the best student in class.
words.ex_cn: 他无疑是班上最好的学生。
words.en: Without doubt; certainly.

words.ex: This painting is unique because no other like it exists.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是独特的，因为没有其他类似的。
words.en: Something that is unique is the only one of its kind.

words.ex: The kitchen has a new washing appliance.
words.ex_cn: 厨房里有一台新的洗衣机。
words.en: An appliance is a device or machine that is used to perform a particular task, especially in the home.

words.ex: The witness lost credibility after lying.
words.ex_cn: 证人因撒谎而失去了可信性。
words.en: The quality of being trusted and believed in.

words.tr:
v. 耗尽；用完；使筋疲力尽
n. 排气管；废气
words.ex: The long hike exhausted him.
words.ex_cn: 这次漫长的徒步旅行让他筋疲力尽。
words.en: If something exhausts you, it makes you so tired, either physically or mentally, that you have no energy left.

words.ex: Washing hands can kill germs.
words.ex_cn: 洗手可以杀死病菌。
words.en: A germ is a very small organism that causes disease.

words.ex: He became reflective after reading the old letter.
words.ex_cn: 他读完那封旧信后变得沉思起来。
words.en: If you are reflective, you are thinking deeply about something.

words.tr:
n. 侦察兵；
v. 搜寻；
words.ex: The scout watched the enemy's movement quietly.
words.ex_cn: 侦察兵悄悄观察敌人的动向。
words.en: A scout is someone who is sent to an area of countryside to find out the position of an enemy or to search for a suitable place for a military camp.

words.tr:
v. 剧烈搅动；（使）猛烈翻腾
n. 搅乳器
words.ex: The machine churns the butter in the cream.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器剧烈搅动奶油来制作黄油。
words.en: To churn means to stir or shake milk or cream in order to make butter, or to move something around violently in water or air.

words.ex: Humans domesticated dogs thousands of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 人类几千年前就驯养了狗。
words.en: To domesticate an animal or plant means to bring it under human control in order to provide food, power, or company.

words.ex: It's a coincidence that we both wore blue today.
words.ex_cn: 我们今天都穿了蓝色，真是巧合。
words.en: A coincidence is when two or more similar or related events occur at the same time by chance and without any planning.

words.ex: Water is a basic necessity for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本必需品。
words.en: Something that is necessary or indispensable.

words.ex: The project is ongoing.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正在进行中。
words.en: An ongoing situation has been happening for quite a long time and seems likely to continue for some time in the future.

words.ex: The minister signed the new law.
words.ex_cn: 部长签署了新法律。
words.en: A minister is a person who is in charge of a particular government department or a member of the clergy in some Christian churches.

words.tr:
v. 剩下；留下；依然不变；
n. 遗迹；残余；遗体；
words.ex: Only two cookies remains on the table.
words.ex_cn: 桌上只剩下两块饼干了。
words.en: The parts left over after other parts have been removed, used, or destroyed.

words.ex: Dust particles float in the air.
words.ex_cn: 灰尘微粒漂浮在空气中。
words.en: A particle is a very small piece or amount of something.

words.tr:
n. 带位员；接待员；门房
v. 引领；招待；做招待员
words.ex: The usher showed us to our seats in the theater.
words.ex_cn: 带位员带我们到了剧院的座位。
words.en: An usher is someone who shows people where to sit, especially at a formal event such as a wedding or a concert. As a verb, to usher means to show someone where to go or to lead them somewhere.

words.tr:
v. 颤抖；颤动；发抖
n. 颤抖
words.ex: The leaf quivers in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 树叶在风中颤抖。
words.en: To shake or tremble with a slight rapid motion; a case for carrying arrows.

words.ex: He lives in seclusion in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他住在山里，过着与世隔绝的生活。
words.en: The state of being private and away from other people.

words.ex: The French Revolution changed the government.
words.ex_cn: 法国大革命改变了政府。
words.en: A revolution is a sudden, extreme, or complete change in something, or the act of making such a change.

words.tr: n. 事先形成的看法；先入之见；成见
words.ex: He had a preconception that all teachers are strict.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个先入为主的观念，认为所有老师都很严格。
words.en: An idea or opinion that is formed before you have enough information or experience, or a bias that prevents objective consideration of an issue.

words.ex: The lion lives in the jungle.
words.ex_cn: 狮子生活在丛林中。
words.en: A jungle is a dense, tropical forest that is home to a wide variety of plants and animals.

words.ex: He can identify the bird by its song.
words.ex_cn: 他能通过鸟的叫声识别它。
words.en: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

words.tr:
v. 跛行；蹒跚；瘸着走
adj. 无力的；无生气的
words.ex: He limps after hurting his leg.
words.ex_cn: 他受伤后走路一瘸一拐。
words.en: If someone limps, they walk with difficulty or in an uneven way because one of their legs or feet is hurt.

words.ex: The manifestation of his anger was a loud shout.
words.ex_cn: 他愤怒的显示是一声大喊。
words.en: A manifestation is an event, action, or object that clearly shows or embodies something, especially a theory or an abstract idea.

words.ex: The house has good insulation to keep warm in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有良好的绝缘层以在冬天保暖。
words.en: Insulation is a material or substance that is used to stop heat, electricity, or sound from going from one place to another.

words.ex: The long meeting was tedious.
words.ex_cn: 这场漫长的会议很沉闷。
words.en: If you describe something such as a job, task, or situation as tedious, you mean it is boring and rather frustrating.

words.ex: He underestimated the difficulty of the test.
words.ex_cn: 他低估了考试的难度。
words.en: If you underestimate something, you do not realize how large, great, or serious it is.

words.ex: The autocratic leader made all decisions without asking others.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁的领导人独自做出所有决定，从不询问他人。
words.en: If you describe someone as autocratic, you are criticizing them because they have complete power and make decisions without asking anyone else's advice.

words.ex: The prevalence of flu increased in winter.
words.ex_cn: 流感在冬季更加流行。
words.en: The fact or condition of being prevalent; commonness.

words.ex: He votes in a democratic election.
words.ex_cn: 他在民主选举中投票。
words.en: A democratic country, government, or political system is governed by representatives who are elected by the people.

words.ex: The bacteria multiply quickly.
words.ex_cn: 细菌迅速增加。
words.en: If you multiply one number by another, you add the first number to itself as many times as is indicated by the second number. For example, 2 multiplied by 3 is equal to 6.

words.ex: The ship carries a large cargo of rice.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船运载了大量大米货物。
words.en: Cargo refers to the goods carried by a ship, aircraft, or other large vehicle.

words.ex: He failed the test, but subsequent efforts helped him pass.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，但随后的努力让他通过了。
words.en: Following in time or order; succeeding.

words.tr:
n. 住所；居住处
v. 逗留；“abide”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: His abode is a small house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他的住所是一栋靠近湖边的小房子。
words.en: A place of residence; a home.

words.ex: The food supply was inadequate for the number of people.
words.ex_cn: 食物供应对人数来说是不充分的。
words.en: If something is inadequate, there is not enough of it or it is not good enough.

words.ex: He felt envious when his friend got a new bike.
words.ex_cn: 当他的朋友得到一辆新自行车时，他感到嫉妒。
words.en: If you are envious of someone, you want something that they have.

words.tr: v. （使）停滞；不发展；因不流动而变得污浊
words.ex: The economy began to stagnate after the crisis.
words.ex_cn: 经济在危机后开始停滞。
words.en: If something such as a business or project stagnates, it stops developing or making progress.

words.tr:
n. 前提；先决条件
v. 预先处理；事先准备
words.ex: You must finish homework as a precondition to play games.
words.ex_cn: 你必须完成作业才能玩游戏。
words.en: A precondition is something that must happen or exist before something else can happen.

words.ex: His superiority in math helped him win the contest.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学上的优越让他赢得了比赛。
words.en: If one side in a war or conflict has superiority, it has an advantage over its enemy, for example because it has more soldiers or better equipment.

words.ex: The government provides welfare to poor families.
words.ex_cn: 政府向贫困家庭提供福利。
words.en: The welfare of a person or group is their health, comfort, and happiness.

words.tr:
n. 特点；特性；
adj. 典型的；特有的；
words.ex: Honesty is a key characteristic of a good friend.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一个好朋友的关键特点。
words.en: A characteristic is a quality or feature that is typical of someone or something.

words.ex: I bought a souvenir from the beach.
words.ex_cn: 我从海边买了一个纪念品。
words.en: A souvenir is something which you buy or keep to remind you of a holiday, place, or event.

words.tr: adj. 可比较的；比得上的；类似的；
words.ex: The prices of these two phones are comparable.
words.ex_cn: 这两部手机的价格是可比较的。
words.en: Something that is comparable to something else is similar in size, amount, or quality.

words.ex: The deer walked through the scrub near the hill.
words.ex_cn: 鹿穿过了山边的灌木丛。
words.en: To scrub something means to rub it hard in order to clean it, especially using a stiff brush and water.

words.ex: He used an adhesive to stick the paper on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他用黏合剂把纸贴在墙上。
words.en: An adhesive is a substance used for sticking objects or materials together.

words.ex: They will demolish the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周会拆掉那座旧建筑。
words.en: To demolish something such as a building means to destroy it completely. It can also mean to defeat someone completely in a discussion, argument, or competition.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.tr: adj. 最新的；最近的；新式的
words.ex: He keeps his knowledge up-to-date by reading news every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天读新闻来保持知识的更新。
words.en: Someone or something that is up-to-date has the most recent information or uses the newest methods or equipment.

words.ex: This puzzle is tricky for kids.
words.ex_cn: 这个谜题对孩子来说很棘手。
words.en: If you describe a task or problem as tricky, you mean that it is difficult to deal with and requires careful thinking or skill.

words.ex: The fence is a barrier to animals.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏是动物的障碍。
words.en: A barrier is something such as a rule, law, or policy that makes it difficult or impossible for something to happen or be achieved.

words.tr:
adj. 壮丽的；堂皇的；重大的；总的；
n. 大钢琴；
words.ex: The grand castle stood on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 壮丽的城堡矗立在山上。
words.en: If you describe a building or a piece of scenery as grand, you mean that its size or appearance is very impressive.

words.tr: n. 正相反的事物；[有化] 对映体
words.ex: Australia is the antipode of the United Kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 澳大利亚是英国的对跖点。
words.en: An antipode is a point on the earth's surface which is diametrically opposite to another point; a direct opposite.

words.ex: Eating wholesome food helps you stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 吃有益身心的食物有助于保持健康。
words.en: Conducive to or suggestive of good health and physical well-being.

words.tr: adj. 普遍的；流行的；盛行的；
words.ex: Smoking is prevalent in that country.
words.ex_cn: 在那个国家，吸烟很普遍。
words.en: If a condition, practice, or belief is prevalent, it is common or widespread.

words.ex: He showed great enthusiasm for learning English.
words.ex_cn: 他对学习英语表现出极大的热情。
words.en: Enthusiasm is a strong feeling of excitement and interest in something and a desire to become involved in it.

words.tr: adj. 值得拥有的；令人渴望的；称心如意的；
words.ex: A quiet neighborhood is desirable for families.
words.ex_cn: 安静的社区对家庭来说是值得拥有的。
words.en: Something that is desirable is worth having or doing because it is useful, necessary, or popular.

words.tr: n. 偶然事故；意外事件
words.ex: He saved money for a contingency.
words.ex_cn: 他存钱以备不时之需。
words.en: A contingency is an event or situation that might happen in the future, especially one that could cause problems.

words.tr:
v. 估算；估价；
n. 估价；估算；
words.ex: Can you estimate how long it will take?
words.ex_cn: 你能估算一下需要多长时间吗？
words.en: If you estimate a quantity or value, you make an approximate judgment or calculation of it.

words.tr: adj. 人口统计的；人口的；
words.ex: The survey collected demographic data like age and income.
words.ex_cn: 这项调查收集了年龄和收入等人口统计数据。
words.en: Relating to the structure of populations.

words.ex: It is advisable to wear a helmet when riding a bike.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是明智的。
words.en: If something is advisable, it will avoid problems if you do it.

words.ex: The Earth is divided into two hemispheres: north and south.
words.ex_cn: 地球被分为两个半球：北半球和南半球。
words.en: A hemisphere is one half of the earth, especially the northern or southern half above or below the equator, or the eastern or western half.

words.ex: He gave a reasonable answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个合理的回答。
words.en: Fair and sensible; not excessive or extreme.

words.tr: n. 食物；营养；维持生计
words.ex: Water and food are basic sustenance for life.
words.ex_cn: 水和食物是生命的基本生存物资。
words.en: Sustenance refers to the food and drink that people, animals, and plants need to live and stay healthy. It can also mean the means of maintaining life or supporting existence.

words.ex: The signpost shows the way to the village.
words.ex_cn: 路标指示了去村庄的路。
words.en: A signpost is a post with a sign on it, giving information such as the direction to a place or the distance to it.

words.ex: The gland secrete sweat to cool the body.
words.ex_cn: 腺体分泌汗液来降温。
words.en: If part of a plant, animal, or human secretes a liquid or substance, it produces it.

words.ex: The clever boy solved the math problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个聪明的男孩很快解决了这道数学题。
words.en: Someone who is clever is intelligent and able to understand things easily or plan things well.

words.tr: v. 使浸透；使湿透；使满；使饱和
words.ex: The sponge will saturate if you pour too much water.
words.ex_cn: 如果你倒太多水，海绵会吸满。
words.en: To saturate something means to make it completely wet, or to fill it completely with something so that no more can be added.

words.ex: He uses fertilizer to help his plants grow.
words.ex_cn: 他用肥料帮助植物生长。
words.en: A substance that is added to soil to improve the growth of plants.

words.tr: n. 支持者；拥护者；辩护者
words.ex: He is a proponent of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁能源的支持者。
words.en: A proponent of an idea or course of action is someone who supports it and tries to persuade other people to support it.

words.ex: The box has a rectangle shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子是长方形的。
words.en: A rectangle is a four-sided flat shape where every interior angle is a right angle (90°). Opposite sides are parallel and of equal length.

words.tr: adj. 广大的；广阔的；广泛的；大量的；
words.ex: He has extensive knowledge of history.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有广博的历史知识。
words.en: Something that is extensive covers a wide area or includes a lot of things.

words.ex: The scientist studied genetic traits in plants.
words.ex_cn: 科学家研究了植物的基因特征。
words.en: relating to genes or heredity

words.ex: The teacher showed a specimen of a butterfly.
words.ex_cn: 老师展示了一个蝴蝶标本。
words.en: A specimen is a single thing or example of something, especially one that is used to represent the whole group or type.

words.ex: The relentless rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 无情的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: Someone who is relentless is determined to do something and refuses to give up, even if what they are doing is unpleasant or cruel.

words.ex: He has awareness of the environmental problems.
words.ex_cn: 他意识到环境问题。
words.en: Knowledge or perception of a situation or fact.

words.ex: His assumption was that the train would be on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是火车会准时。
words.en: An assumption is something that you assume to be the case, even without proof.

words.ex: The dog has a long pedigree from champion lines.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗有着来自冠军血统的悠久血统。
words.en: A pedigree is the recorded ancestry or lineage of a person or animal, often used to indicate purity of breed or high social status.

words.ex: He read a biography of Nelson Mandela.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本关于纳尔逊·曼德拉的传记。
words.en: A biography is a detailed description of a person's life. It involves more than just the basic facts like education, work, relationships, and death; it portrays a person's experience of these life events.

words.tr: adj. 无意识的；无知觉的；
words.ex: He was unconscious after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他失去了意识。
words.en: If someone is unconscious, they are not awake, usually because they have had a severe injury or illness.

words.tr: n. 扭曲；歪曲；失真；畸变；
words.ex: The photo showed distortion in the lines.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片中的线条出现了扭曲。
words.en: A distortion is a change, twist, or exaggeration that makes something appear different from the way it really is.

words.tr: adj. 繁荣的；欣欣向荣的；繁茂的； v. “flourish”的现在分词；
words.ex: The town is flourishing after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 这家新工厂开业后，这个小镇变得繁荣了。
words.en: If something is flourishing, it is growing or developing in a healthy or vigorous way, especially as a result of a particularly congenial environment.

words.ex: Many people face unemployment during the economic crisis.
words.ex_cn: 在经济危机期间，许多人面临失业。
words.en: Unemployment refers to the state of being without a job, especially when one is actively seeking employment.

words.tr: n. 扩展；延长期；延伸；电话分机；
words.ex: The company added an extension to its office building.
words.ex_cn: 公司为办公楼加了一个扩建部分。
words.en: An extension is a part that is added to something to make it longer or larger, or the act of adding this part.

words.ex: The air conditioner keeps the room cool.
words.ex_cn: 空调使房间保持凉爽。
words.en: A conditioner is a substance that you put on your hair after you have washed it to make it softer.

words.tr:
n. 相反；
adj. 相反的；
words.ex: The contrary of hot is cold.
words.ex_cn: 热的相反是冷。
words.en: If you say that something is true contrary to other people's beliefs or opinions, you are emphasizing that it is true and that they are wrong.

words.ex: He needs decompression after a long day at work.
words.ex_cn: 他工作一整天后需要减压。
words.en: The process of reducing pressure or the state of having had pressure reduced.

words.ex: He is amenable to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意接受新想法。
words.en: If you are amenable to something, you are willing to do it or accept it.

words.ex: He follows a dietary plan to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循一种饮食计划来保持健康。
words.en: Relating to the diet or the kinds of food that a person, animal, or community habitually eats.

words.ex: My sibling plays soccer every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 我的兄弟/姐妹每个周末都踢足球。
words.en: A sibling is a brother or sister.

words.ex: The government decided to abolish the old law.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定废除这项旧法律。
words.en: If someone in authority abolishes a system or practice, they formally put an end to it.

words.ex: The elephant is gigantic compared to a dog.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象相比狗来说是巨大的。
words.en: If you describe something as gigantic, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: His motivation is to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他的动机是帮助他人。
words.en: Motivation is the enthusiasm or reason for doing something.

words.ex: The recipe calls for a mixture of flour and water.
words.ex_cn: 这个食谱需要一种面粉和水的混合物。
words.en: A mixture is a substance made by combining other substances together.

words.tr:
v. 发射；发起；启动；
n. 发射；投掷；启动；
words.ex: They will launch a rocket tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将发射一枚火箭。
words.en: To launch something means to send it into the air, space, or water, especially with a lot of force or effort, or to start an activity, event, or project.

words.ex: The ship carries a provision of food for the journey.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船为旅程准备了食物供应。
words.en: A provision is a condition or requirement in a legal document. It can also refer to the act of supplying or providing something that is needed.

words.tr: adj. 天生的；先天的；天赋的
words.ex: He has an inborn talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 他天生就有音乐才能。
words.en: An inborn quality or ability is one that you have had naturally since birth.

words.ex: The glass is brittle and breaks easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃很硬但容易碎。
words.en: If something is brittle, it is hard and easily broken.

words.ex: She added bleach to the white shirt to make it brighter.
words.ex_cn: 她往白衬衫里加了漂白剂，让它更亮。
words.en: To bleach something means to make it white or pale by using a chemical or by exposing it to sunlight.

words.ex: The music heightens the feeling of sadness.
words.ex_cn: 音乐加深了悲伤的感觉。
words.en: If something heightens a feeling or if the feeling heightens, the feeling increases in degree or intensity.

words.tr: n. 女权运动；男女平等主义
words.ex: She believes in feminism and wants equal rights for women.
words.ex_cn: 她相信女权主义，希望女性享有平等权利。
words.en: Feminism is the belief and aim that women should have the same rights, power, and opportunities as men.

words.ex: He gave a thoughtful answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个深思的答案。
words.en: If you are thoughtful, you are quiet and serious because you are thinking about something.

words.tr: v. 重获；夺回；收复；回想
words.ex: He tried to recapture his childhood joy.
words.ex_cn: 他试图重新捕捉童年的快乐。
words.en: To recapture something means to catch it again after it has escaped or been lost, or to experience again a feeling or situation that you had in the past.

words.ex: The child mimics her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If someone or something mimics another person or thing, they try to be like them or copy their behavior or characteristics.

words.ex: The speaker will amplify the sound for everyone to hear.
words.ex_cn: 扬声器会放大声音，让每个人都能听到。
words.en: To amplify something means to make it louder, stronger, or more detailed.

words.tr:
n. 流体；流质；
adj. 流动的；
words.ex: Water is a common fluid.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的流体。
words.en: A fluid is a substance that can flow and change its shape easily, such as a liquid or a gas.

words.ex: His talent overshadowed his brother's achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他的才华使他兄弟的成就黯然失色。
words.en: If an unpleasant event or feeling overshadows something, it makes it less happy or enjoyable.

words.tr: v. 恢复；修复；改造（罪犯）
words.ex: The hospital will rehabilitate the injured athlete.
words.ex_cn: 医院将帮助受伤的运动员康复。
words.en: To rehabilitate someone who has been ill or in prison means to help them to live a normal life again. To rehabilitate a building or an area means to improve its condition.

words.tr: v. 调整；使适合；使适应；
words.ex: He adjusted the chair to sit comfortably.
words.ex_cn: 他调整了椅子以便坐得舒服。
words.en: To adjust something means to change it so that it is more effective or appropriate, or so that it fits better.

words.tr: adj. 不足的；缺乏的；有缺陷的
words.ex: The plant is deficient in sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 这株植物缺乏阳光。
words.en: If someone or something is deficient in a particular thing, they do not have the full amount of it that they need.

words.ex: There was a controversy about the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 关于新校规，人们展开了争论。
words.en: A controversy is a disagreement or argument about something that involves many people and generates strong feelings.

words.tr:
adj. 本土的；
n. 土著；本地人；
words.ex: This plant is native to Australia.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物原产于澳大利亚。
words.en: A native of a particular country or region is someone who was born in that country or region.

words.ex: He adheres to his principles even when it's hard.
words.ex_cn: 即使很难，他仍然坚持自己的原则。
words.en: If you adhere to a rule or agreement, you act in the way that it says you should.

words.ex: He tried to suppress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: To suppress something means to prevent it from being expressed, known, or continuing.

words.ex: He received his father's watch as an inheritance.
words.ex_cn: 他收到了父亲留给他的手表作为遗产。
words.en: Inheritance is money or property which you receive from someone who has died.

words.ex: The ghost is invisible to the human eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个鬼魂肉眼看不见。
words.en: If something is invisible, you cannot see it because it is hidden or because it is very difficult to see.

words.tr: v. 使全神贯注；独占；垄断
words.ex: He is engrossed in reading a novel.
words.ex_cn: 他正全神贯注地读一本小说。
words.en: If something engrosses you, it interests you so much that you do not notice anything else.

words.tr: v. 使预先有倾向；使易接受；使易于患（病）
words.ex: Genes can predispose a person to diabetes.
words.ex_cn: 基因可能使人更容易患糖尿病。
words.en: If something predisposes you to think or behave in a particular way, it makes it likely that you will think or behave in that way.

words.ex: Ancient Egypt is one of the oldest civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及是最早的文明之一。
words.en: A civilization is a human society with its own social organization and culture.

words.ex: The family reduced their monthly expenditure.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭减少了每月的开支。
words.en: Expenditure is the spending of money on something, or the money that is spent on something.

words.tr: v. 销声匿迹；突然消失；
words.ex: The magic trick made the coin vanish.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让硬币销声匿迹了。
words.en: If someone or something vanishes, they disappear suddenly or in a way that cannot be explained.

words.ex: Sugar dissolves in water.
words.ex_cn: 糖在水中溶解。
words.en: If a substance dissolves in liquid or if you dissolve a substance, it becomes mixed with the liquid and disappears.

words.ex: I watched a clip of the movie on YouTube.
words.ex_cn: 我在YouTube上看了这部电影的一个片段。
words.en: A clip is a small device, usually made of metal or plastic, that is specially shaped for holding things together. As a verb, to clip means to cut something, especially to make it shorter or neater.

words.ex: The mirror creates an illusion of a bigger room.
words.ex_cn: 镜子制造出房间更大的错觉。
words.en: An illusion is a false idea or belief, especially about yourself or your situation.

words.ex: He bought a luxury car as an extravagance.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆豪华汽车作为奢侈品。
words.en: Extravagance refers to the spending of more money than is reasonable or than you can afford, or the use of more of something than is necessary.

words.ex: The extinction of dinosaurs happened millions of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 恐龙的灭绝发生在数百万年前。
words.en: The state or process of a species, family, or larger group being or becoming extinct.

words.ex: The water in the pond dwindles in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天时，池塘里的水逐渐减少。
words.en: If something dwindles, it becomes smaller, weaker, or less in number.

words.ex: Strong foundations underpin the building.
words.ex_cn: 坚固的地基支撑着这栋建筑。
words.en: To support, strengthen, or provide a foundation for something.

words.ex: The old man is the guardian of his grandchildren.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人是他的孙子孙女的保护人。
words.en: A guardian is someone who has the legal authority and responsibility to take care of someone else, especially a child whose parents have died.

words.ex: The car remained static at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在红灯前静止不动。
words.en: Something that is static does not move or change.

words.ex: The school stores student records in a database.
words.ex_cn: 学校将学生记录存储在数据库中。
words.en: A database is a collection of data that is organized so that it can easily be accessed, managed, and updated.

words.ex: The bright light stimulated her eyes.
words.ex_cn: 强烈的光线刺激了她的眼睛。
words.en: To stimulate something means to encourage it to begin or develop further.

words.ex: His deficiency in math made him struggle in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学上的缺乏让他在课堂上很吃力。
words.en: A deficiency is a lack or shortage of something that is needed.

words.ex: He bought equity in a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了一家科技公司的股票。
words.en: Equity is the quality of being fair and impartial.

words.ex: He was jailed for embezzlement from his company.
words.ex_cn: 他因盗用公司公款而入狱。
words.en: Embezzlement is the act of dishonestly taking or using money that belongs to someone else, especially when it is in your care or belongs to the organization you work for.

words.ex: Parents shouldn't indulge their children's bad habits.
words.ex_cn: 父母不应该放任孩子的坏习惯。
words.en: To indulge means to allow yourself or someone else to have something enjoyable, especially more than is good for you.

words.ex: The teacher gave candy as a reinforcement for good behavior.
words.ex_cn: 老师用糖果作为良好行为的强化物。
words.en: Reinforcement is the process of encouraging or establishing a belief or pattern of behavior, especially by encouragement or reward.

words.ex: The loan requires collateral documents.
words.ex_cn: 这笔贷款需要附属文件。
words.en: Collateral is something pledged as security for repayment of a loan, to be forfeited in the event of a default.

words.ex: He is doing proofreading for his essay.
words.ex_cn: 他正在为他的文章做校对。
words.en: Proofreading is the activity of finding and correcting mistakes in text before it is printed or put online.

words.ex: The food has a bad odour.
words.ex_cn: 这食物有一种难闻的气味。
words.en: An odour is a particular and distinctive smell.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.ex: He stood amid the trees, quiet and still.
words.ex_cn: 他站在树木中间，安静而静止。
words.en: If something is amid other things, it is surrounded by them.

words.ex: The wedding ceremony was beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 婚礼仪式很美丽。
words.en: A ceremony is a formal event held on special occasions such as weddings, graduations, or official functions, often involving traditional or religious rituals.

words.ex: The shirt is made of synthetic fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫是合成纤维制成的。
words.en: Synthetic products are made from chemicals or artificial substances rather than from natural ones.

words.ex: He resents being ignored by his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他怨恨被老板忽视。
words.en: If you resent someone or something, you feel bitter and angry about them.

words.ex: The weather is a determinant of whether we go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 天气是我们是否去远足的决定因素。
words.en: A determinant is a factor which decisively affects the nature or outcome of something.

words.ex: The problem has too much complexity.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题太复杂了。
words.en: Complexity is the state of having many different parts connected or related to each other in a complicated way.

words.tr:
n. 验尸；尸检；事后调查
adj. 死后的；死后发生的
words.ex: The doctor did a postmortem to find the cause of death.
words.ex_cn: 医生做了尸检以查明死因。
words.en: An examination of a dead body to determine the cause of death or the character and extent of changes produced by disease.

words.ex: The forest has abundant water and trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林水源和树木都很丰富。
words.en: If something is abundant, there is a lot of it or it is very common.

words.ex: The volcano erupts suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 火山突然喷发。
words.en: If a volcano erupts, it throws out smoke, fire, and melted rocks.

words.ex: Vegetables are rich in nutrient.
words.ex_cn: 蔬菜富含营养物。
words.en: A nutrient is a substance that is essential for life and growth, such as the vitamins and minerals in food.

words.ex: The map shows geographical features like mountains and rivers.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图显示了山脉和河流等地貌特征。
words.en: Relating to the study of the physical features of the earth and its atmosphere, and of human activity as it affects and is affected by these, including the distribution of populations and resources, land use, and industries.

words.ex: He wears conventional clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿传统服装去上班。
words.en: Conventional ideas, methods, or systems are the ones that are generally accepted and used, and that have been used for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 持久的；不朽的； v. 忍受；“endure”的现在分词；
words.ex: This is an enduring friendship.
words.ex_cn: 这是一段持久的友谊。
words.en: Lasting for a long time; continuing or enduring over a period of time.

words.tr: adj. 唯物论的；物质至上主义的
words.ex: He is materialistic and only cares about money.
words.ex_cn: 他是个唯物论者，只关心钱。
words.en: If you describe a person or society as materialistic, you are critical of them because they attach too much importance to money and material possessions.

words.tr:
adj. 可变的；易变的；
n. 变量；
words.ex: The weather is variable in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天的天气是多变的。
words.en: A variable is something that is likely to vary; something that is subject to variation.

words.tr: adj. 经验主义的；以经验为根据的；
words.ex: The scientist used empirical data to support her theory.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家使用经验数据来支持她的理论。
words.en: Empirical evidence or study relies on practical experience rather than theories.

words.ex: He is slothful and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他懒惰，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as slothful, you mean that they are lazy.

words.ex: The committee meets every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 委员会每周一开会。
words.en: A committee is a group of people who are chosen to do a particular job or make decisions on behalf of a larger group.

words.tr: adj. 近视的；目光短浅的
words.ex: He is short-sighted and needs glasses to see far.
words.ex_cn: 他近视，需要戴眼镜才能看远。
words.en: If someone is short-sighted, they cannot see things clearly that are far away, or they do not plan for the future in a sensible way.

words.ex: He will participate in the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他将参与学校的戏剧演出。
words.en: To take part in an activity or event.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: The hospital received a donation of books.
words.ex_cn: 医院收到了一批书籍捐赠。
words.en: A donation is a gift which is given to a charity or other organization.

words.tr:
n. 模具；霉；
v. 铸造；
words.ex: The clay was poured into the mould to shape the pot.
words.ex_cn: 将黏土倒入模具中以塑造花盆。
words.en: A mould is a hollow container that you pour a liquid or soft substance into, which then becomes solid in the same shape as the container. Mould can also refer to a fungus that grows on old food or on damp surfaces.

words.tr:
v. 谴责；责难；指责
n. 谴责；责难；指责
words.ex: The teacher censured the student for cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师谴责了那个作弊的学生。
words.en: If you censure someone for something that they have done, you tell them that you strongly disapprove of it.

words.tr:
v. 大步行走；跨一大步
n. 大步；步伐
words.ex: He takes a long stride when he walks.
words.ex_cn: 他走路时迈着大步。
words.en: To walk with long, decisive steps in a specified direction.

words.ex: They decided to postpone the meeting until next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定把会议推迟到下周。
words.en: To postpone something means to arrange for it to take place at a later time than was originally planned.

words.ex: The big company owns a subsidiary that makes phones.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司拥有一家生产手机的附属公司。
words.en: A subsidiary is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.

words.ex: The immigrant found a job in the city.
words.ex_cn: 这位移民在城市里找到了一份工作。
words.en: An immigrant is a person who comes to live permanently in a foreign country.

words.tr: adj. 偏远的；隔离的；孤独的； v. 使隔离；“isolate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The village is isolated, far from any city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄很偏远，远离任何城市。
words.en: If something is isolated, it is far away from other places, buildings, or people.

words.tr: n. 战略家；善于筹划部署的人；
words.ex: He is a strategist who plans every move carefully.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位仔细规划每一步的战略家。
words.en: A strategist is someone who is skilled in planning, especially in military, political, or business contexts.

words.ex: The mountain has great prominence in the landscape.
words.ex_cn: 这座山在景观中十分突出。
words.en: If someone or something is in a position of prominence, they are important or well-known.

words.tr: n. 水族馆；水族箱；养鱼缸；
words.ex: We visited the aquarium to see the fish.
words.ex_cn: 我们去水族馆看鱼。
words.en: A tank or building in which fish and other water creatures and plants are kept.

words.ex: Honesty is a good trait.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种好的特性。
words.en: A trait is a particular characteristic, quality, or tendency that someone or something has.

words.ex: The lab technician transcribes the DNA sequence into RNA.
words.ex_cn: 实验室技术员将DNA序列转录成RNA。
words.en: To transcribe something means to write it down or to copy it from one form of recording to another.

words.tr:
v. 意思是说；表示…的意思；
n. 手段；方法；收入；
words.ex: This sign means you cannot park here.
words.ex_cn: 这个标志意思是说这里不能停车。
words.en: Means refers to a method or way of doing something, or the resources or assets available for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The extra chair is redundant because we have enough seats.
words.ex_cn: 这把额外的椅子是多余的，因为我们已经有足够的座位了。
words.en: If you are made redundant, your employer tells you to leave because your job is no longer necessary or because there is no more work for you.

words.ex: The car made a lateral move to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车横向移动以避开狗。
words.en: Relating to the side or sides; situated at or extending to the side.

words.ex: She is pregnant and will have a baby next month.
words.ex_cn: 她怀孕了，下个月就要生宝宝了。
words.en: Having a baby developing in the uterus.

words.tr: n. 暗指；影射；间接提及
words.ex: He made an allusion to Shakespeare in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中提到了莎士比亚。
words.en: An allusion is an indirect reference to someone or something.

words.tr:
adj. 周期的；定期的
n. 期刊
words.ex: The plant has a periodical blooming cycle.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物有周期性的开花周期。
words.en: A periodical is a magazine, especially one that is published regularly, or something that happens at regular intervals.

words.tr:
v. 溢出；溅出
n. 溢出；溅出
words.ex: He spilled milk on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他把牛奶洒在了地上。
words.en: To cause or allow (a liquid, powder, etc.) to flow or fall out of a container, usually by accident.

words.ex: The simplicity of the design makes it easy to use.
words.ex_cn: 这种设计的简单使它容易使用。
words.en: The quality or condition of being easy to understand or do.

words.ex: He gave a verbal warning instead of a written one.
words.ex_cn: 他给了一个口头警告，而不是书面的。
words.en: Relating to or in the form of words.

words.ex: Birds fly south by instinct.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类凭本能飞向南方。
words.en: An instinct is the natural tendency that a person or animal has to behave or react in a particular way.

words.ex: The auditory system helps us hear sounds.
words.ex_cn: 听觉系统帮助我们听到声音。
words.en: Relating to the sense of hearing.

words.ex: He works hard to emulate his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他努力赶上他的哥哥。
words.en: To emulate someone or something means to try to be like them or to do something in the same way that they do it.

words.ex: Good teachers edify their students with wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 好老师用智慧启发学生。
words.en: To edify someone means to improve their mind or character by teaching them something.

words.ex: He painted a portrait of his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一幅他母亲的肖像。
words.en: A portrait is a painting, drawing, or photograph of a particular person.

words.ex: They accused him of stealing the money.
words.ex_cn: 他们指控他偷了钱。
words.en: If you accuse someone of doing something wrong or dishonest, you say or tell them that you believe that they did it.

words.tr: adj. 不够好的；不能令人满意的；
words.ex: The food was unsatisfactory.
words.ex_cn: 食物不够好。
words.en: If you describe something as unsatisfactory, you mean that it is not as good as it should be, and cannot be considered acceptable.

words.ex: The team went on an expedition to the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍去山上探险了。
words.en: An expedition is an organized journey that is made for a particular purpose such as exploration.

words.ex: The relevance of this topic is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这个主题的相关性是明显的。
words.en: The quality or state of being closely connected or appropriate.

words.ex: It is muggy outside today.
words.ex_cn: 今天外面闷热。
words.en: If you describe the weather as muggy, you mean that it is unpleasantly warm and damp.

words.tr: adj. 痉挛的；间歇的；一阵阵的
words.ex: He had spasmodic coughing at night.
words.ex_cn: 他晚上有阵发性的咳嗽。
words.en: Something that is spasmodic happens suddenly and irregularly, often in short periods of time.

words.ex: He is an earnest student who always finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个认真的学生，总是完成作业。
words.en: If you are earnest about something, you are serious about it and your intentions are honest and sincere.

words.ex: The river overflowed and broke the embankment.
words.ex_cn: 河水泛滥，冲垮了堤坝。
words.en: An embankment is a thick wall of earth that is built to carry a road or railway over an area of low ground, or to prevent water from a river or the sea from flooding an area.

words.tr: v. 焚化；焚毁；把…烧成灰烬
words.ex: The city will incinerate the trash tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市明天将焚烧垃圾。
words.en: To incinerate something means to burn it until it is reduced to ash.

words.ex: He is an expert in the domain of artificial intelligence.
words.ex_cn: 他是人工智能领域的专家。
words.en: A domain is a particular field of thought, activity, or interest, especially one over which someone has control, influence, or rights.

words.ex: He has a high fever as a symptom of the flu.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧是流感的症状。
words.en: A symptom is a physical or mental feature which is regarded as indicating a condition of disease, particularly such a feature that is apparent to the patient.

words.ex: The roller coaster gave her a thrill.
words.ex_cn: 过山车让她感到兴奋。
words.en: A thrill is a sudden feeling of great excitement, pleasure, or fear.

words.ex: He makes occasional visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他偶尔去看望祖父母。
words.en: Occasional means happening or done sometimes, but not regularly or often.

words.tr:
adj. 崇高的；壮丽的；极端的；过分的
v. 变高尚；升华
n. 庄严；崇高；顶点
words.ex: The view from the mountain is sublime.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色是壮丽的。
words.en: If you describe something as sublime, you mean that it has a wonderful quality that affects you deeply.

words.tr: adj. 黑暗的；幽暗的；忧郁的；沮丧的
words.ex: The room was gloomy with no windows.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间没有窗户，很黑暗。
words.en: If a place is gloomy, it is almost dark so that you cannot see very well. If people are gloomy, they are unhappy and have no hope.

words.ex: The barren land cannot grow any crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片贫瘠的土地无法种植任何庄稼。
words.en: If you describe something as barren, you mean that it is not able to produce anything, especially plants or crops.

words.tr: n. 恶名；坏名声；声名狼藉
words.ex: The criminal gained notoriety for his bold robberies.
words.ex_cn: 这名罪犯因大胆的抢劫而声名狼藉。
words.en: Notoriety is the state of being famous or well known for something bad.

words.ex: The moon has a periodic cycle of phases.
words.ex_cn: 月亮的相位变化是周期性的。
words.en: Happening or appearing at regular intervals.

words.ex: The teacher will not condone cheating in exams.
words.ex_cn: 老师不会容忍考试作弊。
words.en: To condone something means to accept or allow behavior that is considered wrong.

words.ex: The movie shows a supernatural ghost.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一个超自然的幽灵。
words.en: Relating to phenomena that cannot be explained by natural laws and are therefore attributed to a divine agency.

words.tr: adj. 侮辱的； v. “insult”的现在分词；
words.ex: His insulting words made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 他侮辱的话让她哭了。
words.en: If you describe someone's remarks or actions as insulting, you mean they are rude and offensive.

words.ex: His recipe for success is hard work and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的秘诀是努力工作和耐心。
words.en: A recipe is a list of ingredients and a set of instructions that tell you how to cook something.

words.ex: The old cemetery is near the church.
words.ex_cn: 那个古老的墓地在教堂附近。
words.en: A cemetery is a place where dead people are buried.

words.tr: adj. 大规模的；大范围的
words.ex: The company started a large-scale project to build new roads.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司启动了一个大规模的项目来修建新道路。
words.en: Involving or affecting a large number of people or things; extensive.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；尚未处理的；
words.ex: He is an outstanding student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名杰出的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as outstanding, you think that they are very remarkable and impressive.

words.ex: He uses an unorthodox method to teach math.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种非传统的方法教数学。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour, beliefs, or customs as unorthodox, you mean that they are different from what is generally accepted.

words.ex: The pink hat on the man looked like an incongruity.
words.ex_cn: 男人头上的粉红色帽子显得很不协调。
words.en: The state of being incongruous; incompatibility.

words.ex: The baby suckles from its mother.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿吸吮母亲的乳汁。
words.en: To suckle means to feed a baby or young animal from the breast or udder.

words.ex: The moon looks like a crescent tonight.
words.ex_cn: 今晚的月亮像一弯新月。
words.en: A crescent is a curved shape that is wider in the middle and pointed at the ends, like the shape of the moon in its first or last quarter.

words.ex: There are many shops on this avenue.
words.ex_cn: 这条大街上有许多商店。
words.en: An avenue is a wide street or main thoroughfare, often lined with trees or other landscaping.

words.ex: He ate a moderate amount of food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了适量的食物。
words.en: If you moderate something or if it moderates, it becomes less extreme or violent, or if you moderate a discussion, you help the people in it to reach an agreement.

words.ex: The glass broke into small fragments.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃碎成了小碎片。
words.en: A fragment of something is a small piece or part of it.

words.ex: He hesitates to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他犹豫着是否要寻求帮助。
words.en: If you hesitate, you pause slightly while you are doing something or just before you do it, usually because you are uncertain, embarrassed, or worried.

words.tr: adj. 令人吃惊的； v. “startle”的现在分词；
words.ex: The news was startling to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息让所有人都感到吃惊。
words.en: Something that is startling is so surprising, unexpected, or remarkable that it makes you feel slightly shocked.

words.ex: The city's sprawl has covered many farmlands.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的杂乱无序的拓展覆盖了许多农田。
words.en: If you sprawl somewhere, you sit or lie with your legs and arms spread out in a careless way.

words.ex: The dress gave her a lot of glamour.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子给她增添了许多魅力。
words.en: If someone or something has glamour, they are attractive and exciting in a way that is not ordinary.

words.tr: n. 对应物；相当之物；副本；
words.ex: The CEO's counterpart in China signed the agreement.
words.ex_cn: 中国方面的对应人物签署了协议。
words.en: Someone's or something's counterpart is another person or thing that has a similar function or position in a different place.

words.ex: The university conferred an honorary degree on him.
words.ex_cn: 大学授予他一个荣誉学位。
words.en: To confer something such as a degree or an honor on someone means to give it to them in a formal way. To confer with someone means to discuss something with them in order to make a decision.

words.tr: adj. 说得过去的；站得住脚的；可防守的
words.ex: His excuse was a little weak, but still tenable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口有点牵强，但还是说得过去的。
words.en: If an idea, argument, or plan is tenable, it is reasonable and could be successfully defended against criticism.

words.ex: He is a so-called expert, but he knows little.
words.ex_cn: 他是个所谓的专家，但懂得很少。
words.en: used to show that something or someone is commonly designated by the name or term specified, often to suggest that the name or term is not appropriate or accurate

words.ex: The movie aroused his curiosity.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影激起了他的好奇心。
words.en: If something arouses a particular reaction or attitude in people, it causes them to have that reaction or attitude.

words.ex: Farmers use pesticide to kill insects on crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民使用杀虫剂来杀死作物上的昆虫。
words.en: A pesticide is a chemical substance used to kill pests, especially insects, that damage crops or are harmful to human health.

words.tr: adj. 令人毛骨悚然的，令人害怕的；<美>令人沮丧的，泄气的；使人感到寒冷的; v. （使）冷却，...
words.ex: The chilling sound of the wind made everyone shiver.
words.ex_cn: 令人毛骨悚然的风声让所有人都颤抖了。
words.en: If you describe something as chilling, you mean it is frightening.

words.ex: The movie was fantastic!
words.ex_cn: 这部电影极好！
words.en: If you describe something as fantastic, you are emphasizing that you think it is very good or that you like it a lot.

words.ex: The school values diversity in its students.
words.ex_cn: 学校重视学生的多样性。
words.en: The state of being diverse; variety.

words.ex: The storm was formidable and destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴很可怕，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as formidable, you mean that you feel slightly frightened by them because they are very great or impressive.

words.ex: He bind the books with string.
words.ex_cn: 他用绳子把书捆起来。
words.en: To tie something or someone tightly or to fasten something.

words.ex: The coach endorses the new player.
words.ex_cn: 教练支持这位新球员。
words.en: If you endorse someone or something, you say publicly that you support or approve of them.

words.ex: He used an analogy to explain how the heart works.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个类比来解释心脏是如何工作的。
words.en: If you make or draw an analogy between two things, you show that they are similar in some way.

words.tr: adj. 匀称的；神智健全的；通情达理的；明智的，头脑清醒的；营养均衡的
words.ex: The sculpture is well-balanced and looks beautiful from every side.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕塑匀称美观，从各个角度看都很漂亮。
words.en: A well-balanced thing is arranged or organized in a way that is sensible, fair, or effective.

words.ex: The king will bestow a medal on the hero.
words.ex_cn: 国王将把奖章授予这位英雄。
words.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

words.ex: Water is indispensable for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必不可少的。
words.en: Absolutely necessary or essential.

words.ex: The default setting is on.
words.ex_cn: 默认设置是开启的。
words.en: If a person, company, or country defaults on something that they have legally agreed to do, such as paying a debt or keeping to an agreement, they fail to do it.

words.tr: adj. 随意的；非正式的；偶然的；
words.ex: He wore casual clothes to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了随意的衣服去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude or behavior as casual, you mean they are not very concerned about what they are doing or what is happening around them, or they are not taking it seriously.

words.tr:
v. 补充；与…相辅相成；
n. 补足物；补语；余角；
words.ex: The red scarf complements her blue coat.
words.ex_cn: 这条红围巾补充了她的蓝外套。
words.en: To complement something means to make it complete or perfect by adding something to it.

words.ex: He waved a patriotic flag during the parade.
words.ex_cn: 他在游行中挥舞着一面爱国的旗帜。
words.en: If someone is patriotic, they feel love, loyalty, and respect for their country.

words.ex: The riot broke out after the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后爆发了骚乱。
words.en: A riot is a violent disturbance of the peace by a crowd.

words.ex: He is a conservative man who likes old traditions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢古老传统的保守男子。
words.en: A conservative person or group is one that does not like changes or new ideas, especially in politics or religion.

words.tr:
v. 挖洞；钻进；翻寻
n. 地洞
words.ex: The rabbit burrows under the tree.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在树下打洞。
words.en: A burrow is a hole or tunnel dug by a small animal, such as a rabbit or a mole, as a dwelling. As a verb, to burrow means to dig a hole or tunnel for habitation or refuge.

words.ex: He finds peace through spiritual meditation.
words.ex_cn: 他通过精神上的冥想找到平静。
words.en: Relating to the human spirit or soul as opposed to material or physical things.

words.ex: The meek boy quietly listened to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 那个温顺的男孩静静地听老师讲课。
words.en: If you describe a person as meek, you think that they are gentle and quiet, and likely to do what other people say.

words.ex: He is the recipient of the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个奖项的接受者。
words.en: A recipient is a person who receives something.

words.ex: The mayor walks to work every morning.
words.ex_cn: 市长每天早上步行上班。
words.en: The mayor of a town or city is the person who has been elected to represent it for a fixed period of time, or, in some places, to run its government.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.tr: adj. 有刺的；有倒钩的；讽刺的
words.ex: The fence has barbed wire on top.
words.ex_cn: 围栏顶部有带刺的铁丝。
words.en: Having a sharp point or points, especially one that is designed to catch or hold something.

words.ex: The ad induced him to buy the product.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告诱使他购买了该产品。
words.en: To induce a state or condition means to cause it.

words.ex: The teacher used a pointer to show the map on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一根指物棒指着墙上的地图。
words.en: A pointer is a piece of advice or information which helps you to understand a situation or to find a way of making progress.

words.tr:
adj. 有生命的；有活力的
v. 使具活力；做成动画
words.ex: The cartoon characters are animate and full of energy.
words.ex_cn: 这些卡通角色是有生命的，充满活力。
words.en: To animate something means to give it life or to make it lively and energetic.

words.ex: The benevolent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位慈善的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: If you describe a person in authority as benevolent, you mean that they are kind and fair.

words.ex: The boat travels along the coastline.
words.ex_cn: 船沿着海岸线航行。
words.en: The coastline is the outline of a coast, especially its shape and appearance.

words.tr: adj. 恐怖的；令人震惊的
words.ex: The accident was horrific.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故非常可怕。
words.en: If you say that something is horrific, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant and shocking.

words.ex: He wore a decent shirt to the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件像样的衬衫去面试。
words.en: Decent is used to describe something which is considered to be of an acceptable standard or quality.

words.tr:
n. 化合物；
adj. 复合的；混合的；
words.ex: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
words.ex_cn: 水是由氢和氧组成的化合物。
words.en: A compound is a substance that consists of two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions.

words.ex: Eating fruits and vegetables is nutritious.
words.ex_cn: 吃水果和蔬菜是有营养的。
words.en: Nutritious food contains substances which help your body to be healthy.

words.ex: The medicine helped revive the sick man.
words.ex_cn: 这剂药帮助这位病人恢复了生机。
words.en: To revive something means to bring it back to life, consciousness, or use, or to make it active or successful again.

words.ex: Water is vital for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you say that something is vital, you mean that it is necessary or very important.

words.tr:
adj. 爆炸的；
n. 炸药；
words.ex: The explosive material was handled with care.
words.ex_cn: 爆炸性材料被小心地处理。
words.en: An explosive substance is capable of causing an explosion. It can also refer to something that is likely to cause an outburst or a sudden increase in activity or emotion.

words.ex: He added the bibliography at the end of his report.
words.ex_cn: 他在报告末尾添加了参考书目。
words.en: A bibliography is a list of the books and articles that have been used by someone when writing a particular book or article.

words.tr: adj. 阴险的；潜伏的；暗中作祟的
words.ex: The insidious virus spread quietly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 这种隐蔽的病毒悄然在小镇蔓延。
words.en: Proceeding in a gradual, subtle way, but with harmful effects.

words.tr: adj. 现实的；现实主义的；
words.ex: He made a realistic plan to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个现实的存钱计划。
words.en: If you are realistic about a situation, you recognize and accept its true nature and try to deal with it in a practical way.

words.tr: n. 迷宫；错综复杂的曲径；
words.ex: The children got lost in the maze.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A maze is a complex system of paths or passages in which it is easy to get lost.

words.ex: The child loves to play with fantasy stories about dragons.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子喜欢玩关于龙的幻想故事。
words.en: A fantasy is a pleasant situation or event that you imagine, which is unlikely to happen.

words.ex: He wields his knowledge to solve problems.
words.ex_cn: 他运用自己的知识来解决问题。
words.en: To wield something means to hold and use it, especially as a weapon or tool. It can also mean to have and be able to use power or influence.

words.ex: The factory reduced wastage by improving its machines.
words.ex_cn: 工厂通过改进机器减少了损耗。
words.en: Wastage refers to the loss of something as a result of it being used or the process of losing something by using it.

words.ex: The old bridge will disintegrate if no one fixes it.
words.ex_cn: 如果没人修理，这座旧桥会瓦解。
words.en: If something disintegrates, it breaks into many small pieces or parts and is destroyed.

words.ex: He is an apprentice in a car repair shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是汽车修理店的一名学徒。
words.en: An apprentice is a young person who works for someone in order to learn their skill.

words.ex: He uses this park exclusively for walking.
words.ex_cn: 他只在这个公园散步。
words.en: If you do something exclusively, you do it only in the way mentioned, and not in any other way.

words.tr:
n. 痛苦；折磨；令人痛苦的东西
v. 折磨；使痛苦；烦扰；纠缠；戏弄
words.ex: The loss of his dog was a deep torment.
words.ex_cn: 失去他的狗是一种深深的痛苦。
words.en: Torment refers to severe physical or mental suffering, or to cause someone to experience such suffering.

words.tr: adj. 下意识的；潜意识的；
words.ex: The ad used subliminal messages to influence buyers.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告使用了下意识的信息来影响买家。
words.en: Subliminal refers to something that is below the threshold of sensation or consciousness; it is perceived by or affecting someone's mind without their being aware of it.

words.ex: There is a restriction on smoking in this building.
words.ex_cn: 这栋楼里禁止吸烟。
words.en: A restriction is an official rule that limits what you can do or that limits the amount or size of something.

words.ex: His metabolism is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 他的新陈代谢非常快。
words.en: Metabolism is the set of life-sustaining chemical transformations within the cells of living organisms.

words.tr:
v. 跌倒；摔倒；暴跌
n. 摔倒；混乱；暴跌
words.ex: The child tumble down the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 孩子从楼梯上跌倒了。
words.en: If someone or something tumbles, they fall quickly and suddenly, often turning over or spinning as they fall.

words.tr: adj. 善于操纵的；会控制的；
words.ex: He is a manipulative person who always controls others.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个善于操纵他人的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as manipulative, you disapprove of them because they skillfully force or persuade people to act in the way that they want.

words.tr: adj. 逃避的；推托的；闪烁其辞的
words.ex: He gave an evasive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个回避的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as evasive, you mean that they deliberately avoid giving clear direct answers to questions.

words.tr: adj. 有独创性的；巧妙的；
words.ex: The child came up with an ingenious way to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子想出了一个有独创性的方式来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Something that is ingenious is very clever and involves new ideas, methods, or equipment.

words.ex: This temperature is the optimum for growing plants.
words.ex_cn: 这个温度是最适宜植物生长的。
words.en: The optimum is the best or most favorable condition, degree, amount, etc., for achieving a particular result.

words.ex: The refinement of the machine made it faster.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的改进使它更快了。
words.en: Refinement is the process of making a substance pure or the quality of being polite, well-educated, and able to judge the quality of things.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.tr: v. 使痛苦；“afflict”的现在分词；
words.ex: The illness is afflicting many old people.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病正在使许多老人受苦。
words.en: If something afflicts you, it causes you physical or mental suffering.

words.ex: The painting is considered a masterpiece by art critics.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画被艺术评论家视为杰作。
words.en: A masterpiece is a work of art such as a painting, film, or book that is made with great skill and is considered to be the best work of a particular artist or writer.

words.ex: He stood in the midst of the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他站在人群中间。
words.en: The middle part or point of something.

words.tr: n. 认可；识别；认识；承认；
words.ex: His hard work got recognition from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力得到了老板的认可。
words.en: The action or process of recognizing or being recognized, in particular.

words.ex: They erect a flagpole in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们在公园里竖立一根旗杆。
words.en: If people erect something such as a building, bridge, or barrier, they build it or create it.

words.ex: He felt miserable after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到很悲惨。
words.en: If you are miserable, you are very unhappy.

words.ex: The government started a crackdown on illegal drugs.
words.ex_cn: 政府开始对非法毒品进行严厉打击。
words.en: A crackdown is a series of severe measures taken to restrict or suppress undesirable or illegal people or behavior.

words.tr: n. 内向的人；不喜欢与人交往的人
words.ex: He is an introvert who likes reading alone.
words.ex_cn: 他是个喜欢独自读书的内向者。
words.en: An introvert is a person who tends to shrink from social contacts and to become preoccupied with their own thoughts.

words.ex: The signal transmission is clear and strong.
words.ex_cn: 信号传输清晰而强劲。
words.en: The act or process of sending or passing something from one place, person, or thing to another.

words.tr:
n. 探测器；
v. 探查；
words.ex: The probe sent back photos from Mars.
words.ex_cn: 探测器从火星传回了照片。
words.en: If you probe into something, you ask questions or try to discover facts about it. A probe is also a long thin instrument that doctors and dentists use to examine parts of the body.

words.tr: v. 装入胶囊；压缩；简述；概括
words.ex: The pharmacist encapsulate the medicine into small capsules.
words.ex_cn: 药剂师把药物装入小胶囊中。
words.en: To encapsulate something means to express or show the most important facts about it in a very short and clear form.

words.ex: He drew a geometric shape on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上画了一个几何图形。
words.en: Relating to geometry, or according to its methods and principles.

words.ex: They did a collaborative project in class.
words.ex_cn: 他们在课堂上做了一个合作项目。
words.en: A collaborative piece of work is done by two or more people or groups working together.

words.ex: The book has a finite number of pages.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的页数是有限的。
words.en: Something that is finite has a definite fixed size or extent.

words.ex: He tried to disprove the theory with new data.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用新数据驳斥这个理论。
words.en: To disprove something means to show that it is not true or correct.

words.ex: The job position is still vacant.
words.ex_cn: 这个职位仍然空缺。
words.en: If something is vacant, it is not being used by anyone.

words.tr: adj. 令人苦恼的； v. “distress”的现在分词；
words.ex: The news was distressing for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息对每个人来说都是令人苦恼的。
words.en: Causing anxiety, sorrow or pain; upsetting.

words.tr:
v. 交配繁殖；饲养；
n. 品种；
words.ex: The farmers breed cows to get more milk.
words.ex_cn: 农民让奶牛交配繁殖以获得更多牛奶。
words.en: If you breed animals or plants, you keep them for the purpose of producing more animals or plants with particular qualities, in a controlled way.

words.ex: The steps must be followed in sequential order.
words.ex_cn: 这些步骤必须按顺序进行。
words.en: Sequential means relating to or following in a sequence.

words.tr: n. 企业家；创业者；承包人；
words.ex: He is an entrepreneur who started a small coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位创办了小型咖啡店的企业家。
words.en: An entrepreneur is a person who organizes and operates a business or businesses, taking on greater than normal financial risks in order to do so.

words.ex: He gropped in the dark for the light switch.
words.ex_cn: 他在黑暗中摸索着找电灯开关。
words.en: If you grope for something that you cannot see, you try to find it by moving your hands around in order to feel it.

words.ex: This jacket is waterproof.
words.ex_cn: 这件夹克是防水的。
words.en: Something that is waterproof does not let water pass through it.

words.ex: The wind propels the sailboat forward.
words.ex_cn: 风推动帆船前进。
words.en: To propel something in a particular direction means to cause it to move in that direction.

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.ex: The manager will empower the team to make decisions.
words.ex_cn: 经理将授权团队做决定。
words.en: To give someone the authority or power to do something.

words.tr:
v. 闪烁；隐约闪现
n. 亮光；闪光
words.ex: The sun gleams on the water.
words.ex_cn: 阳光照在水面上，闪闪发亮。
words.en: A gleam is a small, bright light, especially one that shines for a short time.

words.tr:
vt. 连接；把……互相连结
n. 连环
words.ex: The roads interlink the small towns.
words.ex_cn: 这些道路将各个小镇连接在一起。
words.en: to connect or link together

words.ex: The baby ate the tender broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝吃了嫩的西兰花。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as tender, you mean that they are kind, gentle, and sympathetic. If meat or other food is tender, it is easy to cut or chew. To tender something such as a service or a resignation means to formally offer or present it.

words.ex: His main shortcoming is being late often.
words.ex_cn: 他的主要缺点是经常迟到。
words.en: A shortcoming is a fault or a failure to meet a certain standard, which means a person or thing is not as good as they should be.

words.ex: The doctor suggested a natural remedy for the cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议了一种治疗感冒的天然疗法。
words.en: A remedy is a cure or a way of making something better.

words.ex: The recalcitrant student refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个顽抗的学生拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as recalcitrant, you mean that they are unwilling to obey orders or are difficult to deal with.

words.tr: adv. 急剧地；引人注目地；
words.ex: The temperature dropped dramatically overnight.
words.ex_cn: 夜间温度急剧下降。
words.en: In a way that is sudden, noticeable, or significant, often in a way that is intended to produce a strong effect.

words.tr:
adj. 第一手的；直接的；
adv. 第一手地；直接地；
words.ex: He got firsthand information from the witness.
words.ex_cn: 他从目击者那里获得了第一手信息。
words.en: obtained directly from the original source

words.tr:
n. 烈火；火焰；闪耀
v. 闪耀；熊熊燃烧；发亮光
words.ex: The fire began to blaze in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 火在森林里开始猛烈燃烧。
words.en: A blaze is a very large or fiercely burning fire that is difficult to control.

words.ex: He is weak-willed and gives up easily.
words.ex_cn: 他意志薄弱，容易放弃。
words.en: Lacking the strength of will to act decisively or resolutely.

words.ex: The results were statistically significant.
words.ex_cn: 这些结果在统计上是显著的。
words.en: In a way that relates to statistics or the use of statistics.

words.ex: He believes in an egalitarian society where everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他相信一个人人平等的平等主义社会。
words.en: Egalitarian is used to describe something that is based on the principle that all people are equal and deserve equal rights and opportunities.

words.ex: The poison in the snake is a natural toxin.
words.ex_cn: 蛇的毒液是一种天然毒素。
words.en: A toxin is a poisonous substance, especially one produced by bacteria, which causes disease.

words.tr:
v. （使）纠缠；使陷入；使混乱
n. 纠缠；混乱；纠纷
words.ex: The cat got into a tangle with the yarn.
words.ex_cn: 猫和毛线缠在一起了。
words.en: If something is tangled or tangles, it becomes twisted together in an untidy way.

words.tr: adj. 单调乏味的；毫无变化的；
words.ex: The work is monotonous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作单调乏味。
words.en: Something that is monotonous is very boring because it has a regular, repeated pattern which never changes.

words.ex: Smoking can imperil your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会危及你的健康。
words.en: To put someone or something at risk of being harmed, damaged, or destroyed.

words.ex: The family had a reunion last Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 这家人上个星期天举行了团聚。
words.en: A reunion is a gathering of people who have been separated, especially members of a family or old friends, coming together again.

words.tr: adj. 引人注目的；显著的； v. 打击；“strike”的现在分词；
words.ex: The painting has a striking color scheme.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有着引人注目的配色。
words.en: Something that is striking is very noticeable or unusual.

words.tr:
n. 影响力；冲击（力）；
v. 对…产生影响；
words.ex: The new law had a big impact on education.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律对教育产生了重大影响。
words.en: The effect or influence of one person, thing, or action, on another.

words.ex: He swallowed the pill with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水吞下了药片。
words.en: To swallow means to make food or drink go down your throat and towards your stomach. It can also mean to accept something without protest or to believe something too easily.

words.tr: v. 强烈吸引住；使着迷；
words.ex: The magic show fascinated the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演深深吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If something fascinates you, it interests and delights you so much that your thoughts tend to concentrate on it.

words.tr: n. 承包商；承包人；订约人
words.ex: The contractor fixed the roof last week.
words.ex_cn: 承包商上周修好了屋顶。
words.en: A contractor is a person or company that undertakes a contract to provide materials or labor to perform a service or do a job.

words.ex: The weather will deteriorate tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天天气会恶化。
words.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

words.ex: He has an insatiable hunger for knowledge.
words.ex_cn: 他对知识有着无法满足的渴望。
words.en: If someone is insatiable, they always want more of something and are never satisfied.

words.ex: Calling time a thief is a metaphor.
words.ex_cn: 把时间称为小偷是一种隐喻。
words.en: A metaphor is a figure of speech in which a word or phrase is applied to an object or action to which it is not literally applicable.

words.tr: v. 反复灌输；谆谆劝导
words.ex: Parents try to inculcate good habits in their children.
words.ex_cn: 父母试图在孩子身上培养良好的习惯。
words.en: To inculcate is to teach and impress by frequent repetitions or admonitions.

words.tr: adj. 中等的；次要的；第二的；
words.ex: He attends a secondary school in the city.
words.ex_cn: 他在城里上一所中学。
words.en: If you describe something as secondary, you mean that it is less important than something else.

words.ex: The team's cohesion helped them win the match.
words.ex_cn: 团队的凝聚力帮助他们赢得了比赛。
words.en: Cohesion refers to the action or fact of forming a united whole, especially in the context of a group of people or the parts of a substance.

words.ex: His participation in the meeting was very important.
words.ex_cn: 他参与会议非常重要。
words.en: The act of taking part in something.

words.tr: adj. 可想象得出的；可信的；可能的
words.ex: It is conceivable that he will arrive late.
words.ex_cn: 他可能会迟到，这是可以想象的。
words.en: Capable of being imagined or grasped mentally.

words.tr: phrase. 卡片目录（用于图书馆中按卡片索引图书的系统）
words.ex: He found the book using the card catalogue.
words.ex_cn: 他通过卡片目录找到了这本书。
words.en: A card catalogue is a system for organizing information about the books and other materials in a library, consisting of cards with information on them that are arranged in a particular order.

words.tr:
n. 经常重复的评价（或抱怨）；叠句；
v. 克制；
words.ex: His constant refrain is that the food is too expensive.
words.ex_cn: 他经常抱怨食物太贵。
words.en: If you refrain from doing something, you deliberately do not do it.

words.ex: The statue will immortalise the hero.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像将使这位英雄永垂不朽。
words.en: To immortalise someone or something means to make them famous for a very long time, often by creating a work of art or literature about them.

words.tr:
n. 膨胀；凸出部分；暴涨
v. 膨胀；凸出；急增
words.ex: The balloon begins to bulge when filled with air.
words.ex_cn: 气球充气时开始鼓起来。
words.en: If something bulges, it sticks out or swells in a rounded shape.

words.ex: His loyalty to his friends never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的忠诚从未改变。
