words.ex: He uses deductive reasoning to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他使用演绎推理来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Deductive reasoning is a logical process in which a conclusion is based on the concordance of multiple premises that are generally assumed to be true.

words.ex: The police will detain the suspect for questioning.
words.ex_cn: 警察将扣留嫌疑人进行审问。
words.en: If someone is detained, they are officially held in a place, especially a prison, and are not allowed to leave.

words.ex: He bought the car impulsively.
words.ex_cn: 他有推动力地买了那辆车。
words.en: If you describe someone as acting impulsively, you mean that they act suddenly without thinking carefully about what they are doing, often because they are being controlled by their emotions.

words.ex: The lunatic was taken to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 那个疯人被送到了医院。
words.en: A lunatic is someone who behaves in a crazy or very foolish way.

words.ex: The police used surveillance to watch the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察使用监视来观察那栋大楼。
words.en: The careful watching of a person or place, especially by the police or army, because of a crime that has happened or is expected.

words.ex: The drawback of this phone is its short battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的缺点是电池续航时间短。
words.en: A drawback is a feature of something that makes it less useful or desirable than it could be.

words.ex: He composes music in his spare time.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间创作音乐。
words.en: To compose something means to make it by combining parts or elements.

words.tr:
v. 转移；转让；调任；
n. 转移；转让；调任；
words.ex: He will transfer the money to his bank account.
words.ex_cn: 他将把钱转到他的银行账户。
words.en: If you transfer something or someone from one place to another, or they transfer from one place to another, they go from the first place to the second.

words.ex: He tried to resist the temptation to eat sweets.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抵制吃甜食的诱惑。
words.en: If you resist something such as a change, you refuse to accept it and try to prevent it.

words.ex: The minority group voted for change.
words.ex_cn: 少数群体投票支持变革。
words.en: A minority is a group of people within a community or country who are different from the majority of the people there in race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.ex: The house has three storeys.
words.ex_cn: 这栋房子有三层。
words.en: A storey is a level of a building; a floor.

words.ex: The truck is laden with boxes.
words.ex_cn: 这辆卡车装满了箱子。
words.en: If someone or something is laden with a lot of heavy things, they are holding or carrying them.

words.ex: His conceit makes him ignore others' advice.
words.ex_cn: 他的自负让他忽视别人的建议。
words.en: An excessively favorable opinion of one's own abilities or worth; vanity.

words.ex: The scarcity of water caused problems in the village.
words.ex_cn: 水的缺乏给村庄带来了问题。
words.en: A scarcity of something is a situation in which there is not enough of it.

words.ex: He bought an extravagant car that cost too much money.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆奢侈的车，价格太贵了。
words.en: Spending much more than is necessary or wise; excessively expensive.

words.tr:
n. 海峡；渠道；河床；频道；
v. 引导；
words.ex: The English Channel separates England from France.
words.ex_cn: 英吉利海峡将英格兰与法国分隔开。
words.en: A channel is a television station and the programs that it broadcasts. A channel is also a method or system that people use to send information, goods, etc. to each other.

words.ex: The police discovered a scheme to steal money.
words.ex_cn: 警方发现了一个偷钱的阴谋。
words.en: A scheme is a plan or arrangement, especially one produced by a government or other organization, or a secret plan to do something, especially something illegal or dishonest.

words.ex: The train's destination is Beijing.
words.ex_cn: 这列火车的目的地是北京。
words.en: The place to which someone or something is going or being sent.

words.ex: He compresses the file to save space.
words.ex_cn: 他压缩文件以节省空间。
words.en: To compress something means to press it or squeeze it so that it takes up less space.

words.ex: The storm was destructive and broke many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴具有破坏性，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: Causing great and irreparable harm or damage.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊其词的；难以解释的
words.ex: His answer was equivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可。
words.en: If you are equivocal, you are deliberately vague in what you say, because you want to avoid speaking the truth or making a decision.

words.ex: He gave an affirmative answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了肯定的回答。
words.en: An affirmative word or gesture indicates agreement or consent.

words.ex: The court will prosecute him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将因盗窃罪起诉他。
words.en: To prosecute means to institute legal proceedings against someone or to carry on a legal action against a defendant in a court of law. It also means to continue with or carry on an activity or enterprise.

words.ex: The new regime changed the tax laws.
words.ex_cn: 新的管理制度改变了税法。
words.en: A regime is the set of rules or the way that a country or organization is governed, especially when it is considered to be strict or unfair.

words.tr: adj. 不安全的；危险的；不稳当的；
words.ex: The ladder was precarious and might fall.
words.ex_cn: 梯子不安全，可能会倒。
words.en: If a situation is precarious, it is uncertain or dangerous, and could get worse or fail.

words.ex: The mysterious box appeared on his doorstep.
words.ex_cn: 那个神秘的盒子出现在他的门口。
words.en: If someone or something is mysterious, it is not fully understood or explained and seems interesting or puzzling.

words.tr:
n. 光泽；上光剂；
v. 擦亮；润色；
words.ex: The polish of the wooden table made it shine.
words.ex_cn: 木桌的光泽让它闪闪发亮。
words.en: If you polish something, you make it smooth and shiny by rubbing it with a cloth or a special substance. Polish is also a substance that you use to make things smooth and shiny.

words.ex: He will resit the math exam next month.
words.ex_cn: 他下个月将重考数学考试。
words.en: If someone resits an examination, they take it again, usually because they failed it the first time.

words.tr:
v. 移栽；移植；
n. 移植；
words.ex: He will transplant the flowers to the garden tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天要把这些花移栽到花园里。
words.en: To transplant something means to move it from one place to another. In medicine, to transplant an organ, piece of skin, etc. means to use it to replace a damaged part in someone's body.

words.ex: His comprehension of the story was very good.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个故事的理解很好。
words.en: Comprehension is the ability to understand something.

words.ex: The company will publicise the new product next week.
words.ex_cn: 公司将在下周宣传新产品。
words.en: To publicise something means to make it widely known to the public, especially by using the media.

words.ex: A shudder ran through her when she saw the snake.
words.ex_cn: 当她看到蛇时，全身战栗了一下。
words.en: If you shudder, you shake with fear, horror, or disgust, or because you are cold.

words.ex: The boy is a piano prodigy at age six.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩六岁时就是一位钢琴奇才。
words.en: A prodigy is someone who is unusually young and has a great natural ability in a particular area.

words.ex: The appendix contains extra data for the report.
words.ex_cn: 附录包含了报告的额外数据。
words.en: An appendix is a section at the end of a book that contains additional information. It can also refer to the small tube attached to the large intestine in the human body, known as the vermiform appendix.

words.ex: The poison is lethal to humans.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒药对人类是致命的。
words.en: Something that is lethal can kill people or animals.

words.ex: He opposes the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他反对这项新法律。
words.en: If you oppose someone or something, you disagree with them and try to prevent them from doing something, or you try to change what they are doing.

words.tr:
n. 毒药；毒物；
v. 毒害；
words.ex: The snake's poison can kill quickly.
words.ex_cn: 蛇的毒药能迅速致死。
words.en: A poison is a substance that causes harm or death if it is swallowed, absorbed, or breathed in. It can also refer to something that has a very harmful effect on something else.

words.ex: The cable connects the computer to the printer.
words.ex_cn: 这条电缆将电脑连接到打印机。
words.en: A cable is a thick wire or rope, or a bundle of wires or ropes, used to carry electricity or electronic signals, or to support a structure.

words.ex: The weather prediction says it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 天气预测说明天会下雨。
words.en: A prediction is a statement about what you think will happen in the future.

words.tr:
n. 研究生；
adj. 大学毕业后的；
words.ex: He is a postgraduate at Beijing University.
words.ex_cn: 他是北京大学的一名研究生。
words.en: A postgraduate is a student who continues studying after obtaining a first degree, usually in order to obtain a higher qualification.

words.ex: Her mornings are hectic with work and kids.
words.ex_cn: 她的早晨因为工作和孩子而紧张忙碌。
words.en: If you describe a situation as hectic, you mean that it is very busy and involves a lot of rushed activity.

words.ex: The two roads diverge after the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 两条路在桥后分岔。
words.en: If one thing diverges from another similar thing, the first thing becomes different from the second or develops differently from it. You can also say that two things diverge.

words.ex: The defendant spoke calmly in court.
words.ex_cn: 被告在法庭上平静地发言。
words.en: A defendant is a person or entity against whom a criminal or civil action is brought in a court of law.

words.tr:
v. 投入；跳入
n. 跳进；骤降
words.ex: He plunged into the cold water.
words.ex_cn: 他跳进了冰冷的水里。
words.en: If something or someone plunges in a particular direction, especially into water, they fall, rush, or throw themselves in that direction.

words.tr:
v. 藏匿；隐藏
n. 一批贮藏物
words.ex: He stashes his money under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他把钱藏在床底下。
words.en: If you stash something valuable in a secret place, you store it there to keep it safe.

words.ex: The disadvantage of living far away is long commute time.
words.ex_cn: 住得远的劣势是通勤时间长。
words.en: A disadvantage is a factor which makes someone or something less useful, acceptable, or successful than other people or things.

words.ex: They decided to relocate to a quieter town.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定搬到一个更安静的城镇。
words.en: to move to a new place and establish one's home or business there

words.ex: The city needs better infrastructure for roads and water.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市需要更好的道路和供水设施。
words.en: The basic physical and organizational structures and facilities (e.g., buildings, roads, power supplies) needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.

words.ex: He enquired about the train schedule.
words.ex_cn: 他询问了火车时刻表。
words.en: If you enquire about something, you ask for information about it.

words.ex: He showed great concentration while solving the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在解这道数学题时非常专注。
words.en: Concentration is the ability to focus all your attention on one thing without being distracted.

words.tr:
adj. 秘密的；隐蔽的
n. （动物可藏身的）小树丛
words.ex: He made a covert plan to leave without telling anyone.
words.ex_cn: 他秘密制定了一个不告诉任何人就离开的计划。
words.en: Covert activities or situations are secret or hidden.

words.ex: He sent a letter of condolence to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他给朋友寄了一封慰问信。
words.en: An expression of sympathy, especially on the occasion of a death.

words.ex: The students handed in a petition to the principal.
words.ex_cn: 学生们向校长递交了一份请愿书。
words.en: A petition is a document signed by a lot of people which asks a government or other official group to do a particular thing.

words.tr:
n. 元帅；高级军官；典礼官；消防局长
v. 整理；集结
words.ex: The marshal led the army into battle.
words.ex_cn: 元帅率领军队上战场。
words.en: A marshal is a high-ranking officer in the armed forces, especially in the army or air force, or a person who arranges or directs a public event.

words.tr:
n. 艰苦跋涉；
v. 长途跋涉；
words.ex: The trek across the mountains took five days.
words.ex_cn: 穿越群山的艰苦跋涉花了五天时间。
words.en: A trek is a long and often difficult journey, especially one made on foot.

words.ex: He bought insurance for his car.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的车买了保险。
words.en: Insurance is an arrangement in which you pay money to a company, and they pay money to you if something unpleasant happens to you, for example if your property is stolen or damaged, or if you get a serious illness.

words.ex: The police opened an enquiry into the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方对这起事故展开了调查。
words.en: An enquiry is a question you ask in order to get some information.

words.ex: The respondent answered all the questions honestly.
words.ex_cn: 这位调查对象诚实地回答了所有问题。
words.en: A respondent is someone who replies to something such as a survey or set of questions.

words.ex: The surgeon fixed the broken bone.
words.ex_cn: 外科医生修复了断裂的骨头。
words.en: A surgeon is a medical doctor who performs operations.

words.ex: He will enroll in the English course next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周将注册英语课程。
words.en: To officially register or enlist oneself or someone else in a course, institution, or organization.

words.ex: The new app is an offshoot of the original website.
words.ex_cn: 这个新应用是原网站的衍生物。
words.en: An offshoot is something that has developed from something larger or more general.

words.ex: He envisions a world without war.
words.ex_cn: 他想象一个没有战争的世界。
words.en: To envision something is to imagine it as a future possibility; it is often used to describe the act of foreseeing or planning for the future.

words.ex: The chair has a wobble on one leg.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子有一条腿在晃动。
words.en: If something wobbles or if you wobble it, it moves unsteadily from side to side.

words.ex: The new car outstrips the old one in speed.
words.ex_cn: 这辆新车在速度上超过了旧车。
words.en: To outstrip means to go faster or to do better than someone or something else.

words.ex: He was punished for plagiarism in his essay.
words.ex_cn: 他因论文剽窃而受到惩罚。
words.en: Plagiarism is the practice of using or copying someone else's idea or work and pretending that you thought of it or created it.

words.ex: The essence of love is caring for others.
words.ex_cn: 爱的本质是关心他人。
words.en: The essence of something is its basic and most important characteristic which gives it its individual identity.

words.tr: adj. 适合居住的；可居住的；
words.ex: The planet is habitable because it has water and air.
words.ex_cn: 这颗行星有水和空气，适合居住。
words.en: A place that is habitable is suitable or good enough for people to live in.

words.ex: The frequency of the radio station is 101.5 MHz.
words.ex_cn: 这个电台的频率是101.5兆赫。
words.en: The rate at which something happens or is repeated over a particular period of time.

words.ex: The foundation gives money to poor students.
words.ex_cn: 这个基金会向贫困学生提供资金。
words.en: The foundation of something such as a belief or way of life is the things on which it is based.

words.ex: I anticipate rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我预料明天会下雨。
words.en: If you anticipate an event, you realize in advance that it may happen and you are prepared for it.

words.ex: The bustle of the market filled the morning air.
words.ex_cn: 市场的喧哗充满了早晨的空气。
words.en: If someone bustles somewhere, they move there in a hurried way, often because they are very busy or excited.

words.ex: The company's revenue increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的收入去年增加了。
words.en: Revenue is the income that a company, organization, or government receives regularly.

words.ex: The rain will retard the construction of the road.
words.ex_cn: 雨水会延迟道路的建设。
words.en: To retard something means to delay it or make it happen more slowly than it would otherwise.

words.tr: adj. 公正的；不偏不倚的；
words.ex: The judge was impartial in the trial.
words.ex_cn: 法官在审判中是公正的。
words.en: Someone who is impartial is not directly involved in a particular situation, and is therefore able to give a fair opinion or decision about it.

words.ex: The room has good ventilation through the windows.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间通过窗户有良好的通风。
words.en: The provision of fresh air to a room, building, etc., or the system that does this.

words.ex: He felt disappointment when he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 当他考试没及格时，他感到失望。
words.en: A feeling of sadness or displeasure caused by the nonfulfillment of one's hopes or expectations.

words.ex: His residence is near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他的住所靠近公园。
words.en: A residence is a house or place where someone lives.

words.ex: He inferred that she was tired from her yawns.
words.ex_cn: 他从她的哈欠推断出她很累。
words.en: If you infer that something is the case, you decide that it is true on the basis of information that you already have.

words.ex: His enrolment at the university starts next month.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学的入学时间是下个月。
words.en: Enrolment refers to the process of signing up or registering for something, such as a school, course, or program.

words.ex: The empire ruled many countries long ago.
words.ex_cn: 这个帝国很久以前统治了许多国家。
words.en: An empire is a group of countries or territories that are under the control of a single ruler or government.

words.ex: The engineer built a prototype of the new car.
words.ex_cn: 工程师制作了这辆新车的原型。
words.en: A prototype is the first or original example of something that has been or will be copied or developed; it is a model or preliminary version.

words.ex: The document is confidential and cannot be shared.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件是机密的，不能分享。
words.en: If you talk to someone in a confidential way, you talk to them quietly because what you are saying is secret or private.

words.ex: The circumference of the circle is 31.4 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个圆的周长是31.4厘米。
words.en: The circumference of a circle is the distance around it.

words.tr: n. 前任；前辈；原有事物
words.ex: He became the new manager, replacing his predecessor.
words.ex_cn: 他成为了新经理，接替了他的前任。
words.en: A predecessor is someone who had a job or a position before someone else, or something that comes before another thing in time or in a series.

words.ex: The small village lies on the periphery of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个小村庄位于城市的外围。
words.en: The outer limits or edge of an area or object.

words.tr: n. 羽毛球运动；羽毛球；
words.ex: He plays badminton every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每周末打羽毛球。
words.en: A game played with rackets and a shuttlecock, which is hit back and forth across a high net.

words.ex: The attraction of the city draws many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: An attraction is something that makes people want to go to a place or do a particular thing because they are interested in it.

words.ex: The music accompanies the dance.
words.ex_cn: 音乐伴随舞蹈。
words.en: To go somewhere with someone as a companion or escort; to play a musical accompaniment for.

words.ex: The retailer sells clothes to customers.
words.ex_cn: 这家零售商向顾客出售衣服。
words.en: A retailer is a person or business that sells goods to the public in relatively small quantities for use or consumption rather than for resale.

words.ex: It is advantageous to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 早起是有利的。
words.en: If something is advantageous to you, it is likely to benefit you.

words.ex: The fierce lion chased the deer.
words.ex_cn: 那只凶猛的狮子追赶着鹿。
words.en: A fierce animal or person is very aggressive or angry.

words.ex: His handwriting is illegible.
words.ex_cn: 他的字迹无法辨认。
words.en: If something is illegible, it is impossible to read because the letters or characters are not clear, are not formed properly, or are obscured in some way.

words.ex: He didn't flinch when the needle touched his skin.
words.ex_cn: 当针碰到他的皮肤时，他没有退缩。
words.en: If you flinch, you make a small sudden movement, especially when something surprises you or hurts you.

words.tr: adj. 感觉不到的；极细微的
words.ex: The change was imperceptible to the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个变化肉眼无法察觉。
words.en: Something that is imperceptible is so small or slight that it cannot be seen or noticed.

words.tr: n. 含意；可能的影响（或后果）；暗示；
words.ex: The implication of his words was that he was sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他话中的含意是他很抱歉。
words.en: An implication is a possible future effect or result of an action or decision, often one that is not immediately obvious.

words.ex: His belief in honesty never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对诚实的信念从未改变。
words.en: A belief is a strong feeling that something is true or exists.

words.ex: Asia is the largest continent.
words.ex_cn: 亚洲是最大的洲。
words.en: A continent is a very large area of land, such as Africa or Asia, that consists of several countries.

words.ex: The team comprises five players and one coach.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队包括五名球员和一名教练。
words.en: If you say that something comprises or is comprised of a number of things or people, you mean it has them as its parts or members.

words.tr: n. 奢华；奢侈品；难得的享受；
words.ex: She bought a luxury dress for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一件奢华的裙子。
words.en: Luxury is very great comfort, especially among beautiful and expensive surroundings.

words.ex: He offended the law by stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他偷窃触犯了法律。
words.en: If you offend someone, you upset or embarrass them by saying or doing something that they think is rude or insulting.

words.ex: He tries to invert the numbers to find the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他试图将数字倒过来以找到答案。
words.en: To invert something means to turn it upside down or to reverse its position, order, or relationship.

words.tr: v. 使麻痹；使瘫痪；使无效；使停止活动
words.ex: The accident paralyzed his leg.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他的腿瘫痪了。
words.en: If someone is paralyzed by an accident or an illness, they have no feeling in their body, or in part of their body, and are unable to move.

words.tr:
v. 逝去；过去
n. （光阴）逝去
words.ex: Two hours elapsed while he waited for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他等公交车时，两个小时过去了。
words.en: If time elapses, it passes.

words.ex: He will surrender when he sees the police.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到警察时，他会投降。
words.en: If you surrender, you stop fighting or resisting someone and agree that you have been beaten.

words.tr:
v. 根深蒂固地记住；生染
adj. 根深蒂固的；染色的
words.ex: Parents try to ingrain good habits in their children.
words.ex_cn: 父母试图在孩子心中根植良好的习惯。
words.en: To fix beliefs or ideas in someone's mind so firmly that they are unlikely ever to be forgotten or changed.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；主要的；基本的；最好的；
words.ex: This is the prime reason for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 这是延误的首要原因。
words.en: Prime is used to describe something that is of the best possible quality, or the most important or basic part of something.

words.ex: He dismissed her advice and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会她的建议，走开了。
words.en: If you dismiss someone, you send them away or allow them to leave.

words.ex: He possesses a small house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有一栋靠近湖边的小房子。
words.en: If you possess something, you have it or own it.

words.ex: The meeting was fruitful and solved many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议富有成效，解决了许多问题。
words.en: Producing good or helpful results; productive.

words.tr: adj. 充满热情的；热心的；
words.ex: He is enthusiastic about playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他对打篮球充满热情。
words.en: If you are enthusiastic about something, you show how much you like or enjoy it by the way that you behave and talk.

words.tr:
n. 预测；预报；
v. 预测；预报；
words.ex: The weather forecast says it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 天气预测说明天会下雨。
words.en: If you forecast future events, you say what you think is going to happen in the future.

words.ex: The motion of the ball is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 球的运动非常快。
words.en: The action or process of moving or being moved.

words.tr: v. 断言；宣称；坚持；维护
words.ex: He asserts that the answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持认为答案是正确的。
words.en: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.

words.ex: The ship arrived at the dock at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 船在日出时到达了码头。
words.en: A dock is an enclosed area of water in a port where ships go to be loaded, unloaded, and repaired.

words.ex: He was arrested for perpetrating a fraud.
words.ex_cn: 他因实施诈骗而被逮捕。
words.en: If someone perpetrates a crime or any other immoral or harmful act, they do it.

words.ex: Please inform me when the meeting starts.
words.ex_cn: 请在会议开始时通知我。
words.en: To inform someone means to tell them about something.

words.tr:
adj. 最初的；开始的；
n. 首字母；
words.ex: This is the initial plan for the project.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个项目的最初计划。
words.en: The first letter of a name or word, used to represent the whole name or word.

words.ex: This painting has a distinctive style.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有独特的风格。
words.en: Something that is distinctive has a special quality or feature which makes it easily recognizable and different from other things of the same type.

words.tr:
adj. 漫长而艰难的；
adv. 朝上坡方向；
words.ex: Losing weight is an uphill task for many people.
words.ex_cn: 对许多人来说，减肥是一项漫长而艰难的任务。
words.en: If something is uphill, it is going up a slope or hill. If you say that something is uphill, you mean that it is difficult and requires effort.

words.tr:
adj. 居住的；常驻的；
n. 常住居民；
words.ex: The resident population grew last year.
words.ex_cn: 居住人口去年增加了。
words.en: A resident is someone who lives in a particular place or a person who has their home in a place.

words.ex: He uses optical lenses to see small objects.
words.ex_cn: 他使用光学镜片来看小物体。
words.en: Relating to sight, especially in relation to the physical action of light.

words.ex: He is clumsy and dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他很笨拙，把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: A clumsy person moves or handles things in a careless, awkward way, often so that things are knocked over or broken.

words.ex: His speech was coherent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲连贯且易于理解。
words.en: If something is coherent, it is well planned, so that it is clear and sensible and all its parts go well with each other.

words.ex: The desert has a harsh climate.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的气候非常严酷。
words.en: If you describe something as harsh, you mean that it is extremely difficult and unpleasant to live in, do, or experience, especially because it is very cold, hot, or violent.

words.ex: He did it out of spite.
words.ex_cn: 他出于恶意做了这件事。
words.en: If you do something out of spite, you do it because you want to hurt or upset someone.

words.tr:
n. 最小值；
adj. 最小量的；
words.ex: The minimum of the function is 5.
words.ex_cn: 这个函数的最小值是5。
words.en: The minimum is the smallest or least amount possible or allowed.

words.ex: He read the previous chapter last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚读了前一章。
words.en: Existing or occurring before in time or order.

words.ex: The two colors are distinct.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色有区别。
words.en: If something is distinct, it is easily seen, heard, or understood.

words.tr:
n. 避难所；庇护所；
v. 庇护；遮蔽；
words.ex: The refugees found shelter in a small building.
words.ex_cn: 难民们在一个小建筑里找到了避难所。
words.en: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.

words.tr:
v. 皱眉；蹙额
n. 皱眉；蹙额
words.ex: He frowns when he hears bad news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到坏消息时会皱眉。
words.en: If you frown, you bring your eyebrows together so that there are lines on your face above your eyes, often because you are annoyed or worried.

words.ex: The red hat was conspicuous in the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 那顶红帽子在人群中非常显眼。
words.en: Something that is conspicuous is very obvious or easy to notice.

words.ex: He made a commitment to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺按时完成这个项目。
words.en: A commitment is something that regularly takes up some of your time because of an agreement you have made or because of responsibilities that you have.

words.tr:
adj. 成熟的；
v. 成熟；
words.ex: He is a mature student who works full-time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成熟的学生，全职工作。
words.en: When something or someone matures, they become fully grown or developed. In finance, a mature investment is one that has reached the end of its term and is ready to be paid out.

words.ex: The children loved the circus with clowns and elephants.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢有小丑和大象的马戏团。
words.en: A circus is a group of performers that include clowns, acrobats, and trained animals, who travel to different places to entertain people.

words.tr: n. 矛盾心理；正反感情并存
words.ex: He feels ambivalence about moving to a new city.
words.ex_cn: 他对搬到新城市感到矛盾。
words.en: Ambivalence is the state of having mixed feelings or contradictory attitudes about something or someone.

words.ex: He gave a precise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了准确的答案。
words.en: If you give precise information or precise instructions, you give exact details so that there is no confusion about what should be done.

words.ex: The children were exposed to cold weather without coats.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在没有外套的情况下遭受了寒冷天气。
words.en: To expose something means to uncover it so that it can be seen, or to make it known or public.

words.ex: I cannot foresee what will happen tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我无法预知明天会发生什么。
words.en: If you foresee something, you expect and believe that it will happen.

words.tr:
n. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
v. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
words.ex: The abuse of power led to many problems.
words.ex_cn: 权力的滥用导致了许多问题。
words.en: Abuse is the improper usage or treatment of a thing, often to unfairly or improperly gain benefit. Abuse can come in many forms, such as physical or verbal maltreatment, injury, assault, violation, rape, unjust practices, crimes, or other types of aggression.

words.tr: n. 需优先考虑的事；优先权；
words.ex: Homework is my top priority.
words.ex_cn: 作业是我最需要优先考虑的事。
words.en: If something is a priority, it is the most important thing you have to do or deal with, or must be done or dealt with before everything else you have to do.

words.tr: adj. 不顾一切的；极度渴望的；绝望的；
words.ex: He made a desperate attempt to save the child.
words.ex_cn: 他不顾一切地试图救那个孩子。
words.en: If you are desperate, you are in such a bad situation that you are willing to try anything to change it.

words.ex: The loud music was a diversion from his worries.
words.ex_cn: 那嘈杂的音乐分散了他对烦恼的注意力。
words.en: A diversion is an action or event that attracts your attention away from what you are doing or should be doing.

words.ex: The train went through a long tunnel.
words.ex_cn: 火车通过了一条长长的隧道。
words.en: A tunnel is a long passage which has been made under or through the ground, usually through a hill or under a river, to allow people or vehicles to travel through it.

words.ex: The incidence of flu increased last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天流感的发生率上升了。
words.en: The incidence of something is the frequency with which it occurs or the rate at which it happens.

words.tr: n. 公共卫生；卫生设施；
words.ex: The city improved sanitation to keep people healthy.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市改善了公共卫生以保障人民健康。
words.en: The conditions and processes that help maintain health and prevent disease, especially through cleanliness.

words.ex: The violent storm destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场暴力的风暴摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: If someone is violent, or if they do something that is violent, they use physical force or weapons to hurt, injure, or kill other people.

words.tr: adj. 不感兴趣的；不关心的；
words.ex: He was indifferent to the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.tr:
n. 等价物；
adj. 相等的；等价的；
words.ex: The dollar is the equivalent of ten yuan.
words.ex_cn: 美元是十元的等价物。
words.en: If one amount or value is the equivalent of another, they are the same.

words.tr:
n. 委员会；佣金；
v. 委托；
words.ex: The commission met to discuss the new law.
words.ex_cn: 委员会开会讨论新法律。
words.en: A commission is a group of people who have been appointed to find out about something or to control something, or the act of doing this. It can also refer to a sum of money that is paid to someone for selling something, which is usually a percentage of the value of the goods sold.

words.ex: He conform to the rules of the school.
words.ex_cn: 他遵守学校的规章制度。
words.en: To conform means to behave in a way that is accepted by most people or to obey a rule, law, or custom.

words.ex: The painting depicts a quiet village at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一个宁静的村庄在日落时分的景象。
words.en: To depict someone or something means to show or represent them in a work of art such as a drawing or painting.

words.tr: n. 奖金；红利；额外津贴；
words.ex: He received a bonus for working overtime.
words.ex_cn: 他因加班获得了奖金。
words.en: A bonus is an extra amount of money that is added to someone's pay, usually because they have worked very hard.

words.ex: We had a snack and some drinks as refreshment after the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议结束后，我们吃了点心和喝了一些饮料作为茶点。
words.en: Refreshment refers to the act of refreshing or the state of being refreshed, especially by food or drink. It can also mean a light meal or drinks served in a social setting.

words.tr: v. 报（某事）之仇；为（某人）报仇
words.ex: He wants to avenge his brother's death.
words.ex_cn: 他想为弟弟的死报仇。
words.en: To avenge someone means to harm or punish someone who has harmed them or someone they care about.

words.ex: He tries to assimilate new words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力吸收新单词。
words.en: To assimilate means to take in and understand fully ideas, information, or culture, or to make something become part of a group or system.

words.ex: The teacher will determine the winner of the contest.
words.ex_cn: 老师将确定比赛的获胜者。
words.en: If you determine something, you decide it or settle it.

words.ex: My passport will expire next month.
words.ex_cn: 我的护照下个月到期。
words.en: If something such as a contract or a visa expires, it comes to an end or is no longer valid.

words.ex: Prior to the meeting, we reviewed the report.
words.ex_cn: 在会议之前，我们复习了报告。
words.en: Existing or coming before in time, order, or importance.

words.ex: The boy found a fossil in the rock.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在岩石中发现了一块化石。
words.en: A fossil is the remains or impression of a prehistoric organism preserved in petrified form or as a mold or cast in rock.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.ex: His sadness manifested in his quiet eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲伤表现在他安静的眼神中。
words.en: To manifest something means to show it clearly and visibly.

words.ex: The books are on the shelf beside the aisle.
words.ex_cn: 书在过道旁边的架子上。
words.en: An aisle is a long narrow gap that people can walk along between rows of seats in a public building such as a church or between rows of shelves in a supermarket.

words.ex: The farmer's cultivation of rice takes months.
words.ex_cn: 农民种植水稻需要几个月的时间。
words.en: The process of trying to acquire or develop a quality or skill.

words.ex: He did an internship at a hospital last summer.
words.ex_cn: 去年夏天，他在一家医院实习。
words.en: An internship is a period of work experience offered by an organization for a limited period of time. It is typically undertaken by students and graduates looking to gain relevant skills and experience in a particular field.

words.ex: The forest has high biodiversity.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林生物多样性很高。
words.en: Biodiversity refers to the variety of life in the world or in a particular habitat or ecosystem.

words.ex: He remarked that the weather was nice.
words.ex_cn: 他评论说天气很好。
words.en: If you remark that something is the case, you say that it is the case.

words.ex: He sings and plays guitar simultaneously.
words.ex_cn: 他一边唱歌一边弹吉他。
words.en: If two or more things happen simultaneously, they happen at exactly the same time.

words.ex: The body expels waste through the kidneys.
words.ex_cn: 身体通过肾脏排出废物。
words.en: If someone is expelled from a school or organization, they are officially told to leave because they have behaved badly or broken the rules.

words.ex: He keeps his diary private.
words.ex_cn: 他把日记保密。
words.en: If something is private, it is for the use of one person or group, rather than for the general public.

words.ex: The air feels humid after it rains.
words.ex_cn: 雨后空气感觉湿润。
words.en: You use humid to describe an atmosphere or climate that is very damp, and usually very hot.

words.tr: adj. 悲剧的；悲惨的；不幸的；
words.ex: The accident was a tragic event.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故是一场悲剧。
words.en: A tragic event or situation is extremely sad, usually because it involves death or suffering.

words.ex: The small room was cosy with a warm blanket and a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 这个小房间铺着温暖的毯子，喝着热茶，非常舒适。
words.en: A place or situation that is cosy is comfortable and warm.

words.ex: He looks at the bug through a microscope.
words.ex_cn: 他通过显微镜观察这只虫子。
words.en: An instrument used for viewing objects that are too small to be seen by the naked eye, especially one that uses a combination of lenses to produce a magnified image.

words.ex: He ate only a small portion of the cake.
words.ex_cn: 他只吃了一小部分蛋糕。
words.en: A portion of something is a part of it.

words.tr: v. 给予选举权；释放（奴隶）
words.ex: The law will enfranchise all adults over 18.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律将赋予所有18岁以上成年人选举权。
words.en: To enfranchise someone means to give them the right to vote in elections.

words.ex: Don't discourage him from trying.
words.ex_cn: 不要阻止他尝试。
words.en: If someone or something discourages you, they cause you to lose your enthusiasm about your actions.

words.ex: I congratulate you on your success.
words.ex_cn: 我祝贺你取得成功。
words.en: If you congratulate someone, you express pleasure for something good that has happened to them, or you praise them for something they have achieved.

words.ex: He uses logic to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他用逻辑来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Logic is a method of reasoning that involves a series of statements, each of which must be true if the statement before it is true.

words.ex: He asked for assistance with his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他请求帮助做作业。
words.en: The act of helping or supporting someone or something.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；给书籍、杂志等加插图；
words.ex: The teacher illustrated the point with a simple story.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的故事来举例说明这个观点。
words.en: To illustrate something means to explain or demonstrate it clearly, often by giving examples or by using pictures or diagrams.

words.ex: The hospital is a public institution.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院是一家公共机构。
words.en: An institution is a large important organization such as a university, church, or bank.

words.ex: The faculty of engineering has many labs.
words.ex_cn: 工程学院有许多实验室。
words.en: A faculty is a group of departments in a university or college that specialize in a particular subject or group of subjects, or the teachers in such a group.

words.ex: His words had a profound effect on her life.
words.ex_cn: 他的话对她的生活产生了深远的影响。
words.en: If you describe something as profound, you mean that it is very great or intense.

words.ex: This plant is resistant to drought.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物对干旱有抵抗力。
words.en: If someone is resistant to something, they are opposed to it and want to prevent it.

words.ex: The car's velocity increased on the highway.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车在高速公路上的速度增加了。
words.en: Velocity is the speed at which something moves in a particular direction.

words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.tr:
n. 钩；挂钩；
v. 钩住；
words.ex: The key hung on a metal hook.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙挂在金属钩上。
words.en: A hook is a bent piece of metal or plastic that is used for catching or holding things, or for hanging things on.

words.ex: The old ship was a monster on the sea.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船在海上是个庞然大物。
words.en: A monster is an imaginary creature that is very large, ugly, and frightening.

words.ex: The weather is mild today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天气温和。
words.en: Mild is used to describe something that is not extreme, severe, or strong, such as weather, taste, or behavior.

words.ex: The man was punished for fraud.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因欺骗而受到惩罚。
words.en: Fraud is the crime of gaining money or financial benefits by a trick or by lying.

words.tr: v. 驱逐出境；使举止得体
words.ex: They will deport him for breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 他们将因他违法而驱逐他。
words.en: If a government deports someone, usually someone who is not a citizen of that country, it sends them out of the country because they have committed a crime or because it believes they do not have the right to be there.

words.ex: He ate a chunk of cheese for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐吃了一大块奶酪。
words.en: A chunk of something is a large piece or amount of it.

words.ex: Five apples constitute a basket.
words.ex_cn: 五个苹果构成一篮子。
words.en: If something constitutes a particular thing, it can be regarded as being that thing.

words.ex: The barge carried coal down the river.
words.ex_cn: 驳船沿河运送煤炭。
words.en: A barge is a long, flat-bottomed boat used for carrying freight on canals and rivers.

words.tr:
adj. 无数的；
n. 无数；
words.ex: There are myriad stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数的星星。
words.en: A myriad of things or people is a very large number of them.

words.ex: I checked the class schedule for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我查看了明天的课程时间表。
words.en: A schedule is a plan that gives a list of events or tasks and the times at which each one should happen or be done.

words.ex: The construction of the new bridge took two years.
words.ex_cn: 新桥的建筑花了两年时间。
words.en: The process or method of building or making something, especially buildings, bridges, etc.

words.ex: The statistics show a rise in sales last year.
words.ex_cn: 这些统计数字显示去年销售额有所上升。
words.en: Statistics is a branch of mathematics dealing with the collection, analysis, interpretation, presentation, and organization of data.

words.ex: The doctor wrote a prescription for medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了一张药方。
words.en: A prescription is a written order from a physician for the preparation and administration of a drug or device for a patient.

words.ex: This small enterprise makes handmade toys.
words.ex_cn: 这家小企业生产手工玩具。
words.en: An enterprise is a company or business, often a large one, or a difficult or important project, especially one that involves a lot of planning and organization.

words.tr: v. 结晶；定形；（使）具体化；变明确
words.ex: The idea began to crystallize after many talks.
words.ex_cn: 经过多次讨论，这个想法开始明朗起来。
words.en: To crystallize means to cause something to form into crystals or to become clear and definite in form.

words.tr: v. 对…予以惩罚；使处于不利地位
words.ex: The teacher will penalize students who cheat.
words.ex_cn: 老师会惩罚作弊的学生。
words.en: To penalize someone means to punish them or make them suffer in some way because they have done something wrong.

words.tr:
n. 麻烦；困难；争吵
v. 烦扰；纠缠
words.ex: It's not worth the hassle to change your plans.
words.ex_cn: 改变计划不值得这么麻烦。
words.en: If you describe something as a hassle, you mean that it is inconvenient and annoying. As a verb, to hassle someone means to annoy or trouble them persistently.

words.tr: adj. 需要久坐的；惯于久坐不动的；不爱活动的；
words.ex: His sedentary job makes him sit all day.
words.ex_cn: 他的久坐工作让他整天坐着。
words.en: Someone who has a sedentary lifestyle or job sits down a lot of the time and does not take much exercise.

words.ex: He is an emeritus professor at Harvard.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的荣誉教授。
words.en: Emeritus is used to describe a professor, minister, or other professional who has retired but keeps an honorary title corresponding in some way to their former position.

words.ex: The cake has three layers of chocolate.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕有三层巧克力。
words.en: A layer of a substance or material is a quantity or piece of it that covers a surface or that is between two other things.

words.ex: The conflict between the two countries lasted for years.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家之间的冲突持续了多年。
words.en: A conflict is a serious disagreement or argument, typically a protracted one.

words.ex: The mirror distorts my face.
words.ex_cn: 这面镜子扭曲了我的脸。
words.en: If you distort a statement, fact, or idea, you report or represent it in an untrue way.

words.tr: adj. 传导的；能传导（热、电）的
words.ex: Copper is conductive and used in wires.
words.ex_cn: 铜具有导电性，用于电线。
words.en: Having the property of conducting something (especially heat or electricity).

words.ex: He tried to convince her to stay.
words.ex_cn: 他试图说服她留下。
words.en: If someone or something convinces you of something, they make you believe that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: I met him at a party, but he is only an acquaintance.
words.ex_cn: 我在聚会上认识了他，但他只是个熟人。
words.en: An acquaintance is someone you know a little, who is not a close friend.

words.tr:
n. 索具装备；钻探设备；装备
v. 配备索具；操纵；舞弊
words.ex: He uses a rig to hold the camera steady.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个支架来固定相机。
words.en: To rig something means to arrange or set it up in a particular way, often in a temporary or makeshift manner. It can also refer to the equipment used in drilling for oil or gas, or the sails and ropes on a ship.

words.tr:
n. （文字）诽谤
v. 发表文字诽谤（某人）
words.ex: He wrote a false story about her, and it was libel.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于她的虚假文章，这是诽谤。
words.en: A libel is a published false statement that is damaging to a person's reputation; a written defamation.

words.ex: He kept his dignity even when he was poor.
words.ex_cn: 即使他很穷，他依然保持尊严。
words.en: Dignity is the quality of being worthy of honor or respect.

words.ex: He spent the evening in introspection.
words.ex_cn: 他整个晚上都在反省。
words.en: The examination of one's own thoughts, feelings, and sensations; self-examination.

words.ex: He practices his religion every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都实践自己的宗教信仰。
words.en: Religion is the belief in and worship of a superhuman controlling power, especially a personal God or gods.

words.tr:
v. 撞；碰上；颠簸行进；
n. 碰撞；猛击；肿块；凸块；
words.ex: He bumped the table and spilled his drink.
words.ex_cn: 他撞到了桌子，打翻了饮料。
words.en: If you bump into something or someone, you accidentally hit them while you are moving.

words.ex: The smell repels insects.
words.ex_cn: 这种气味能击退昆虫。
words.en: If something repels you, it is so unpleasant or offensive that you want to avoid it or push it away.

words.tr: n. 说明或对白的字幕；副标题；
words.ex: The movie has English subtitles for the dialogue.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影为对白提供了英文字幕。
words.en: A subtitle is a secondary or explanatory title, or a translation of the dialogue in a film or television program, displayed at the bottom of the screen.

words.ex: The celebrity smiled at the fans outside the theater.
words.ex_cn: 这位名人向剧院外的粉丝微笑。
words.en: A celebrity is a famous person, especially in entertainment or sports.

words.ex: He uses inferential statistics to predict the result.
words.ex_cn: 他使用推断统计来预测结果。
words.en: Inferential means relating to or involving inference, which is the process of deriving logical conclusions from premises known or assumed to be true.

words.ex: The company will downsize next month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司下个月将裁员。
words.en: If a company or organization downsizes, it reduces the number of people it employs in order to reduce costs or improve efficiency.

words.tr: v. 复制；复印；再做一次；
words.ex: He duplicated the file to save a copy.
words.ex_cn: 他复制了该文件以保存一份副本。
words.en: To duplicate something means to make an exact copy of it.

words.ex: The luxuriant forest had thick trees and deep green leaves.
words.ex_cn: 这片茂密的森林有茂盛的树木和深绿色的叶子。
words.en: Luxuriant is used to describe something that is rich in growth, abundance, or opulence.

words.ex: Dark clouds portend a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something portends something else, it indicates that it is likely to happen in the future.

words.tr: adj. 艰苦的；强硬的；严厉的；
words.ex: The hike was tough but beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 这次徒步旅行很艰苦但很美丽。
words.en: A tough person is strong and determined, and can tolerate difficulty or suffering.

words.ex: We should conserve water in daily life.
words.ex_cn: 我们应在日常生活中节约用水。
words.en: To conserve something means to protect it from harm, loss, or change, especially in order to preserve it for the future.

words.ex: He pressed the shutter to take a photo.
words.ex_cn: 他按下快门拍了一张照片。
words.en: A shutter is a device used to cover or uncover a window or a camera lens.

words.ex: The locality has many small shops and cafes.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区有许多小商店和咖啡馆。
words.en: A locality is a particular place or area, especially in relation to its geographical position or features.

words.tr:
n. 预算；预算金额；
adj. 廉价的；花钱少的；
v. 为 ... 做预算；
words.ex: We made a budget for our vacation.
words.ex_cn: 我们为旅行制定了一个预算。
words.en: A budget is a plan that shows how much money a person or organization will earn and how much they will need or be able to spend.

words.tr:
v. 拍动；摆动；
n. 薄片；
words.ex: The bird flaps its wings to fly.
words.ex_cn: 鸟拍动翅膀飞翔。
words.en: A flap is a piece of cloth, paper, skin etc that is fixed at one edge to a surface, which you can lift up easily. If something such as a piece of cloth or paper flaps or if you flap it, it moves quickly up and down or from side to side.

words.ex: The storm caused a brutal flood that destroyed many homes.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴引发了残酷的洪水，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: A brutal act or person is cruel and violent.

words.ex: The tree has many colorful ornaments.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树上有许多彩色的装饰品。
words.en: An ornament is an object that is used to make something look more attractive but is usually considered to have no practical purpose.

words.ex: The tribe lives in a primitive hut.
words.ex_cn: 这个部落住在原始的小屋里。
words.en: Belonging to a very early period in the history of the world, or to a time before modern things existed.

words.ex: The map shows the topography of the mountain area.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图显示了山区的地形。
words.en: The topography of an area is the physical features of its surface, such as hills, valleys, and rivers, especially the representation of these features on maps.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；小学的；初等的；原来的；最初的；
words.ex: Primary goal is to stay safe.
words.ex_cn: 首要目标是保持安全。
words.en: Something that is primary is more important than anything else.

words.tr: n. 小路；小巷；航道；车道；航线；
words.ex: The children walked down the narrow lane to school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们沿着狭窄的小路去上学。
words.en: A lane is a narrow road, especially in the country. It can also refer to a division of a road intended to separate lines of traffic moving in the same or opposite directions.

words.ex: He shaves every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上刮胡子。
words.en: To shave means to remove hair from the face or body by cutting it close to the skin with a razor.

words.ex: The lamp emits a soft light.
words.ex_cn: 灯发出柔和的光。
words.en: To emit means to send out something such as light, heat, sound, gas, etc.

words.ex: He achieved mastery of the piano after ten years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 他经过十年的练习，熟练掌握了钢琴。
words.en: If you show mastery of a particular skill or language, you show that you have learned or understood it completely and have no difficulty using it.

words.tr: adj. 过度的；过高的；过分的；
words.ex: The restaurant charged an exorbitant price for a small salad.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅对一份小沙拉要了过高的价格。
words.en: If you describe something such as a price or fee as exorbitant, you are emphasizing that it is much higher than it should be.

words.tr: v. 侵蚀；腐蚀；逐渐丧失；削弱
words.ex: The wind erodes the sand slowly.
words.ex_cn: 风慢慢侵蚀着沙子。
words.en: If rock or soil erodes or is eroded by the weather, sea, or wind, it cracks and breaks so that it is gradually destroyed.

words.ex: The invasive plant spreads quickly and kills other plants.
words.ex_cn: 这种侵入性植物生长迅速，会杀死其他植物。
words.en: If you describe something as invasive, you mean that it spreads very quickly and is difficult to stop.

words.tr:
n. 带扣；皮带扣
v. （使）搭扣扣住
words.ex: The belt has a shiny buckle.
words.ex_cn: 这条皮带有一个闪亮的带扣。
words.en: A buckle is a piece of metal or plastic attached to one end of a belt or strap, which is used to fasten it. As a verb, to buckle means to fasten something with a buckle or to bend or collapse under pressure.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.tr: adj. 一年一次的；每年的；
words.ex: The school holds an annual sports day.
words.ex_cn: 学校每年举行一次运动会。
words.en: An annual event happens once every year.

words.ex: His silence implies he disagrees.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默暗示他不同意。
words.en: To suggest or indicate something indirectly rather than stating it explicitly.

words.ex: The two companies will merge next year.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司明年将合并。
words.en: To combine or unite to form a single entity.

words.ex: The dominant color in the room is blue.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间占优势的颜色是蓝色。
words.en: Someone or something that is dominant is more powerful, successful, influential, or noticeable than other people or things.

words.ex: The ice melts in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 冰在阳光下融化。
words.en: If a solid substance melts or if you melt it, it changes to a liquid, usually because it has been heated.

words.ex: He will flee from the burning house.
words.ex_cn: 他会从着火的房子里逃走。
words.en: If you flee from something or someone, you leave them quickly because you are afraid of them or because you do not want to be involved with them.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.ex: The induction of the new mayor will be held next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 新市长的就职典礼将在下周一举行。
words.en: Induction is the process or action of inducting someone to a position or organization, or the process of reasoning from specific cases to general rules.

words.ex: The steam condenses into water when it touches the cold glass.
words.ex_cn: 当蒸汽接触到冷的玻璃时，会凝结成水。
words.en: If you condense something, especially a piece of writing or a speech, you make it shorter, usually by including only the most important parts.

words.ex: He feigns sleep to avoid talking.
words.ex_cn: 他假装睡觉以避免交谈。
words.en: If someone feigns a particular feeling, attitude, or physical condition, they try to make other people think that they have it or are experiencing it, although this is not true.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；杰出的；罕见的；特别的；
words.ex: She is an exceptional student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 她是一名卓越的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: An exceptional person or thing has some unusual quality or ability that makes them different from others.

words.tr:
n. 纠纷；争端；
v. 对（某事）有异议；
words.ex: The dispute between the two neighbors was about the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间的纠纷是关于篱笆的。
words.en: A dispute is a disagreement or argument about something important.

words.ex: He tried to manipulate the results to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他试图操纵结果来赢得比赛。
words.en: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, often in a way that is considered unfair or dishonest.

words.ex: The baby is crawling on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿正在地板上爬。
words.en: To move slowly on hands and knees or by dragging the body close to the ground.

words.ex: She is flexible with her schedule.
words.ex_cn: 她的日程安排很灵活。
words.en: Able to change or be changed easily according to the situation.

words.ex: She adores her little brother.
words.ex_cn: 她非常喜爱她的弟弟。
words.en: If you adore someone, you feel great love and admiration for them.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.tr:
n. 谓语；述语
v. 使基于；断言；宣布
words.ex: He uses a simple predicate to explain the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个简单的谓语来解释这个句子。
words.en: If you predicate something, you base it on or say that it depends on something else. In grammar, the predicate of a clause is the part of it that is not the subject.

words.ex: The weather can dictate what we wear each day.
words.ex_cn: 天气可以支配我们每天穿什么。
words.en: To dictate means to say or read something aloud for someone else to write down, or to give orders in an authoritative manner.

words.tr: adj. 赤贫的；贫困的；一无所有的；
words.ex: The destitute family had no food or shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这个赤贫的家庭没有食物和住所。
words.en: If you describe someone as destitute, you mean they have absolutely nothing, especially no money.

words.tr: adj. 可获得的；有空的；可用的；
words.ex: The books are available in the library.
words.ex_cn: 这些书在图书馆里可以借到。
words.en: If something is available, it is able to be used or obtained.

words.ex: He took a temporary job during summer.
words.ex_cn: 他在暑假期间做了一份短暂的工作。
words.en: Something that is temporary lasts for only a limited time.

words.tr:
n. 立体声；立体声音响
adj. 立体声的
words.ex: He plays music on the stereo.
words.ex_cn: 他通过立体声收音机播放音乐。
words.en: A stereo is a sound system that uses two or more separate microphones to record sound and two or more loudspeakers to play it back, so that you hear different parts of the sound coming from different directions.

words.ex: The drought made it hard to grow crops.
words.ex_cn: 旱灾使种植庄稼变得困难。
words.en: A drought is a long period of time during which no rain falls and hence there is a shortage of water.

words.tr: v. 制定（法律）；通过（法律）；扮演（角色）
words.ex: The government will enact a new law next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将颁布一项新法律。
words.en: To enact a law or rule means to make it official by passing it through a legislative body.

words.tr: adj. 现代的；当代的；同时代的；
words.ex: This museum displays contemporary art.
words.ex_cn: 这个博物馆展示现代艺术。
words.en: Belonging to or occurring in the present; or a person or thing living or existing at the same time as another.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.ex: The gang tried to extort money from the shop owner.
words.ex_cn: 这个帮派试图向店主敲诈钱财。
words.en: To extort is to obtain something, especially money, through force, threats, or other unfair means.

words.ex: He is grappled with the math problem for hours.
words.ex_cn: 他花了好几个小时努力解决这道数学题。
words.en: To grapple with something means to try hard to understand or deal with a difficult problem or subject.

words.tr: adj. 匆匆的；粗略的；仓促的
words.ex: He gave the report a cursory look.
words.ex_cn: 他粗略地看了看这份报告。
words.en: A cursory glance or examination is a quick one that is not very thorough.

words.ex: He inserts a coin into the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他把一枚硬币放进机器里。
words.en: To put or introduce something into something else.

words.ex: The cat ran down the alley.
words.ex_cn: 猫跑进了小巷。
words.en: An alley is a narrow passage between buildings or other structures.

words.ex: The factory reduces emission to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 工厂减少排放以保护环境。
words.en: An emission is the production and discharge of something, especially gas or radiation.

words.ex: Farmers use irrigation to water their crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民使用灌溉来浇灌庄稼。
words.en: Irrigation is the process of supplying water to land or crops to help growth, typically by means of channels.

words.ex: You need to pay a 40-yuan deposit to rent the bike.
words.ex_cn: 租自行车需要支付40元押金。
words.en: A deposit is a sum of money which is part of the full price of something, and which you pay when you agree to buy it. It is also a sum of money that you pay into a bank account.

words.tr: n. 改造（工程）；建筑改造；整修；
words.ex: The refurbishment of the old school took six months.
words.ex_cn: 这所旧学校的改造工程花了六个月。
words.en: The process of repairing and redecorating something, especially a building, to make it more attractive or functional.

words.ex: The restaurant has a calm ambience.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅有一种宁静的氛围。
words.en: The character and atmosphere of a place.

words.tr:
n. 试验；化验；定量分析
v. 试验；化验；定量分析
words.ex: The lab will assay the blood sample tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 实验室明天将检测这个血液样本。
words.en: An assay is a test to determine the presence, absence, or quantity of one or more components.

words.tr:
n. （统治者的）配偶；一组
v. 厮混；结交
words.ex: The king walked with his consort at the parade.
words.ex_cn: 国王在游行中与他的配偶一起行走。
words.en: A consort is a husband or wife, especially of a reigning monarch. As a verb, it means to habitually associate with someone, typically with the implication of a close or intimate relationship.

words.ex: The castle endured a long siege during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡在战争中经历了长期的围攻。
words.en: A siege is a military operation in which enemy forces surround a town or building, cutting off essential supplies, with the aim of compelling those inside to surrender.

words.ex: The city's expansion caused more traffic.
words.ex_cn: 城市的扩张导致了更多的交通拥堵。
words.en: Expansion refers to the process of becoming larger or more extensive.

words.ex: He flushes the toilet after using it.
words.ex_cn: 他用完厕所后冲水。
words.en: If you flush, your face goes red because you are hot or ill, or because you are feeling a strong emotion such as embarrassment or anger. To flush a toilet means to cause water to pass through it in order to clean it.

words.tr:
n. 连环漫画；
adj. 滑稽的；
words.ex: He reads a comic every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上读一本连环漫画。
words.en: A comic is someone who entertains people by making them laugh, especially a professional comedian.

words.ex: The cows graze in the enclosure.
words.ex_cn: 奶牛在围场里吃草。
words.en: An enclosure is an area that is surrounded by a barrier or fence, often used to keep animals in or to protect something.

words.tr:
n. 恐慌；
v. 感到恐慌；
words.ex: A panic spread through the crowd when the fire alarm rang.
words.ex_cn: 当火警响起时，人群陷入了恐慌。
words.en: Panic is a very strong feeling of anxiety or fear, which makes you act without thinking carefully.

words.tr:
n. 顾虑；顾忌；踌躇
v. 顾虑；有顾忌
words.ex: He had a scruple about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对于对朋友撒谎感到不安。
words.en: A scruple is a feeling of doubt or hesitation with regard to the morality or propriety of a course of action.

words.ex: Interest will accrue over time.
words.ex_cn: 利息会随着时间积累。
words.en: If money or interest accrues, it gradually increases in amount over a period of time.

words.ex: The team's morale improved after they won the game.
words.ex_cn: 球队赢了比赛后，士气提升了。
words.en: Morale is the amount of confidence and cheerfulness that a group of people have.

words.ex: He asked for euthanasia because he was in great pain.
words.ex_cn: 他因为痛苦不堪而要求安乐死。
words.en: Euthanasia is the practice of ending the life of a person or animal in a painless or minimally painful way, usually to relieve suffering from an incurable condition or disease.

words.ex: He will delineate the plan clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地描述这个计划。
words.en: To delineate something means to describe or portray it precisely.

words.tr: adj. 选择性的；精挑细选的；
words.ex: He is selective about what he eats.
words.ex_cn: 他对吃的东西很挑剔。
words.en: If you are selective, you choose things carefully, for example, the things that you buy or do.

words.tr: n. 全体船员；全体人员；
words.ex: The crew fixed the ship's engine during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 全体船员在风暴中修好了船的引擎。
words.en: A crew is a group of people who work on and operate a ship, aircraft, or train.

words.ex: The pilot landed the plane safely.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员安全地降落了飞机。
words.en: A pilot is a person who operates the flying controls of an aircraft. Also, to pilot something means to test or introduce a new idea, product, etc., to see if it will be successful.

words.ex: Many families live in the slum near the city center.
words.ex_cn: 许多家庭住在城市中心附近的贫民窟里。
words.en: A slum is a heavily populated urban area characterized by substandard housing and squalor.

words.tr: n. 养老金；退休金；抚恤金；
words.ex: He receives a monthly pension after retiring.
words.ex_cn: 他退休后每月领取养老金。
words.en: A pension is a sum of money which a retired, widowed, or disabled person regularly receives from the state or from a former employer.

words.ex: The efficacy of the medicine is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物的效果是明显的。
words.en: The ability to produce a desired or intended result.

words.tr: adj. 可笑的；荒谬的；滑稽的
words.ex: It is ludicrous to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套真是荒谬。
words.en: If you describe something as ludicrous, you are emphasizing that you think it is foolish, unreasonable, or unsuitable.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；任性的；乖张的；故意作对的；悖理的
words.ex: He gave a perverse answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个简单的问题给出了一个反常的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as perverse, you mean that they deliberately behave in an unreasonable way, especially by doing the opposite of what is expected or wanted.

words.ex: The trip is contingent on the weather.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅行取决于天气情况。
words.en: A contingent event or situation depends on something else in order to happen or exist.

words.ex: The restaurant serves a famous delicacy called seafood soup.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅供应一道著名的佳肴，叫海鲜汤。
words.en: Delicacy refers to the quality of being delicate, fine, or subtle in appearance, structure, or manner. It can also denote a choice or rare food item.

words.ex: He is aware of the danger.
words.ex_cn: 他意识到危险。
words.en: If you are aware of something, you know about it.

words.ex: The visa application requires a lot of formality.
words.ex_cn: 签证申请需要很多正式手续。
words.en: A formality is something that is done as part of a formal process or procedure, often without much thought or feeling because it is expected.

words.tr:
v. 爆裂；突然而起；
n. 爆裂；突然而起；
words.ex: The balloon burst when he blew too much air.
words.ex_cn: 当他吹入太多空气时，气球爆裂了。
words.en: If something bursts or if you burst it, it suddenly breaks open or splits open and the air or other substance inside it comes out; used especially to describe the sound of something breaking open.

words.ex: He engraves his name on the ring.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在戒指上。
words.en: To engrave means to cut or carve a design or letters into a hard surface, or to be strongly impressed in someone's memory.

words.ex: People discuss politics on this forum.
words.ex_cn: 人们在这个论坛上讨论政治。
words.en: A forum is a place, situation, or group in which people exchange ideas and discuss issues, especially important public issues.

words.ex: He follows a strict regimen to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循严格的作息计划来保持健康。
words.en: A regimen is a systematic plan or course of action intended to improve or maintain health, or a prescribed routine of diet, exercise, or manner of living.

words.ex: He uses homeopathy to treat his cold.
words.ex_cn: 他用顺势疗法治疗感冒。
words.en: Homeopathy is a system of alternative medicine created in 1796 by Samuel Hahnemann, based on his doctrine of like cures like, a claim that a substance that causes the symptoms of a disease in healthy people would cure similar symptoms in sick people.

words.tr:
v. （使）发痒；胳肢；逗乐
n. 痒；胳肢；呵痒
words.ex: The feather tickles my arm.
words.ex_cn: 羽毛挠得我手臂发痒。
words.en: If something tickles you, it touches you in a way that makes you laugh or feel slightly uncomfortable, usually because it is touching a sensitive part of your body. If something tickles you, it also makes you feel amused or pleased.

words.tr: n. 营业额；人员流动率；周转率；
words.ex: The store's turnover increased last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店上个月的营业额增加了。
words.en: The amount of money taken by a business in a particular period.

words.ex: We use a repellent to keep mosquitoes away.
words.ex_cn: 我们使用驱虫剂来驱赶蚊子。
words.en: A repellent is a substance that is used to keep insects or animals away from something. It can also refer to something that is extremely unpleasant or disgusting.

words.ex: He looked at me with confusion.
words.ex_cn: 他困惑地看着我。
words.en: A state of uncertainty about what is happening, intended, or required.

words.ex: The view from the hill is marvellous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色绝妙极了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as marvellous, you are emphasizing that they are extremely good, enjoyable, or impressive.

words.tr: v. 参军；入伍；谋求（某人的帮助）
words.ex: He wants to enlist in the army.
words.ex_cn: 他想参军。
words.en: To enlist means to join the military, or to get someone else to join the military. It can also mean to get support or help from someone for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The police relied on an informant to find the thief.
words.ex_cn: 警察依靠一名信息提供人找到了小偷。
words.en: An informant is someone who gives information to another person or organization, especially information that is secret or private.

words.ex: The stars are visible at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚可以看到星星。
words.en: If something is visible, it can be seen.

words.ex: He had a loud hiccup during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议期间打了个响亮的嗝。
words.en: A hiccup is an involuntary spasm of the diaphragm and respiratory organs, with a sudden closure of the glottis and a characteristic sound.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.ex: He is scrupulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他检查作业时一丝不苟。
words.en: If you are scrupulous, you are careful, thorough, and extremely attentive to details.

words.ex: Workers excavate the old ruins with shovels.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用铲子挖掘古代遗址。
words.en: To excavate means to dig in the ground in order to find things that have been buried there, such as archaeological remains.

words.ex: This decision is pivotal for the company's future.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来至关重要。
words.en: Of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something else.

words.ex: Parents often spoil their children with too many toys.
words.ex_cn: 父母经常用太多玩具宠坏孩子。
words.en: To spoil something means to reduce its quality or value, often by damaging it in some way. It can also mean to treat someone, especially a child, with too much kindness or indulgence, leading to their detriment.

words.ex: The forest is dense with trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林树木茂密。
words.en: Something that is dense contains a lot of things or people in a small area.

words.ex: His opinion coincides with mine.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点与我的一致。
words.en: If one event coincides with another, they happen at the same time.

words.tr:
adj. 精心制作的；详尽的；
v. 精心制作；详尽阐述；
words.ex: She wore an elaborate dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件精心制作的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: To elaborate means to add more details to something that has already been said or written, making it more complex or detailed. As an adjective, it describes something that is very complex and detailed.

words.ex: He defeated his opponent in the chess game.
words.ex_cn: 他在国际象棋比赛中击败了对手。
words.en: An opponent is someone who is competing against you in a contest, game, or argument, or someone who is opposed to an idea or plan.

words.tr:
n. (从事某项活动的)规定期限
v. 吝惜；节省
words.ex: He did a short stint as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他短暂地当过一段时间老师。
words.en: A stint is a fixed period of time during which someone does a particular job or activity.

words.tr:
n. 杂交种；混合物；
adj. 混合的；
words.ex: The corn hybrid grows faster than the old type.
words.ex_cn: 这种玉米杂交种比旧品种长得更快。
words.en: A hybrid is a plant or animal that has been produced from two different types of plant or animal, especially to get better characteristics. It can also refer to something that is a mixture of two different things.

words.ex: He succumbed to the illness after a long fight.
words.ex_cn: 经过长期抗争后，他最终死于疾病。
words.en: If you succumb to temptation, pressure, or something such as an illness, you do something that you want to do, or you give in to the pressure or illness, often after a period of trying not to.

words.ex: The cafe attracts a young clientele.
words.ex_cn: 这家咖啡馆吸引了一群年轻的顾客。
words.en: The clientele of a business or organization are its customers or clients.

words.ex: He packed his paraphernalia before the trip.
words.ex_cn: 他在旅行前收拾好了随身用具。
words.en: The equipment, apparatus, or furnishing used in or necessary for a particular activity.

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.ex: The fishing vessel sailed out at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 那艘渔船在黎明时出海。
words.en: A vessel is a large boat or a container for holding liquids.

words.ex: The pine grows tall in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 松树在森林里长得很高。
words.en: A pine is a type of evergreen tree which has long thin leaves called needles and produces cones. As a verb, to pine means to feel a deep longing or desire for something or someone.

words.ex: He tried to detach himself from the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图脱离这个群体。
words.en: If you detach one thing from another that it is fixed to, you remove it. If one thing detaches from another, it becomes separated from it.

words.ex: The doctor used antiseptic cream on the cut.
words.ex_cn: 医生在伤口上用了防腐药膏。
words.en: An antiseptic is a substance that prevents the growth of disease-causing microorganisms.

words.ex: The keyboard is a peripheral device.
words.ex_cn: 键盘是一个外围设备。
words.en: A peripheral activity or issue is one that is not very important compared with other activities or issues.

words.tr: adj. 黄铜制的；黄铜色的；厚颜无耻的
words.ex: The brazen statue sparkled in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 这尊黄铜雕像在阳光下闪闪发光。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as brazen, you mean that they are doing something shocking or immoral in a very open way, without trying to hide it.

words.tr: n. 高超的技艺；造诣；英勇；
words.ex: His prowess in basketball amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在篮球方面的高超技艺让所有人都惊叹。
words.en: Exceptional skill or ability in a particular field or activity.

words.ex: The detective used forensic evidence to solve the case.
words.ex_cn: 侦探使用法医证据破了案。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the application of scientific methods and techniques to the investigation of crime.

words.ex: The critic praised the new movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位评论家称赞了这部新电影。
words.en: A critic is a person who expresses opinions about the good and bad qualities of books, films, music, etc.

words.ex: His arrogance made others dislike him.
words.ex_cn: 他的傲慢让其他人不喜欢他。
words.en: Arrogance is the quality of being arrogant, which means having or revealing an exaggerated sense of one's own importance or abilities.

words.tr:
n. 腐烂；衰落；
v. 腐烂；
words.ex: The fruit began to show signs of decay.
words.ex_cn: 这水果开始出现腐烂的迹象。
words.en: To decay means to be slowly destroyed by a natural process or to become gradually worse in quality, condition, or strength.

words.tr: adj. 脆弱的；易碎的；不牢固的；
words.ex: The glass is fragile and might break easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个玻璃很脆弱，容易碎。
words.en: If something is fragile, it is easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: The earthquake caused tremendous damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了巨大的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tremendous, you mean that they are very great in amount, extent, or intensity.

words.ex: His ingenuity solved the problem with a simple tool.
words.ex_cn: 他的独创力用一个简单的工具解决了问题。
words.en: Ingenuity is the ability to think of clever and original ways to solve problems.

words.tr: adj. 没有瑕疵或污点的；完好无损的；
words.ex: The diamond was unblemished and sparkled brightly.
words.ex_cn: 这颗钻石没有瑕疵，闪闪发亮。
words.en: If something is unblemished, it has no faults or marks and is perfect in every way.

words.tr:
n. 螺旋形；陡升或骤降；
v. 螺旋式上升（或下降）；
adj. 螺旋形的；
words.ex: The snail moved along a spiral path.
words.ex_cn: 蜗牛沿着一个螺旋形的路径爬行。
words.en: A spiral is a shape which winds round and round, with each curve above or outside the previous one.

words.tr:
v. 没精打采地站（或坐、走）；低头垂肩地站（或坐、走）
n. 没精打采的样子
words.ex: He slouches in his chair while watching TV.
words.ex_cn: 他看电视时驼背坐着。
words.en: If someone slouches, they sit or stand with their shoulders and head bent so that they look lazy and tired.

words.ex: The snake released venom into its prey.
words.ex_cn: 蛇向猎物释放了毒液。
words.en: Venom is a poisonous substance secreted by animals such as snakes and spiders, used for defense or to kill prey.

words.ex: The frog is poisonous.
words.ex_cn: 这只青蛙是有毒的。
words.en: Something that is poisonous will kill you or make you ill if you eat it, drink it, or absorb it.

words.ex: There is friction between the two neighbors over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居因为篱笆问题产生了不和。
words.en: The resistance that one surface or object encounters when moving over another.

words.ex: He lives in a residential area near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他住在公园附近的一个住宅区。
words.en: Relating to or suitable for residence.

words.ex: He had a misconception that the earth is flat.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个错误认识，认为地球是平的。
words.en: A misconception is an idea that is not correct because it is based on a misunderstanding or a wrong belief.

words.ex: He deceived his friend with a lie.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个谎言欺骗了朋友。
words.en: If you deceive someone, you make them believe something that is not true, usually in order to get some advantage for yourself.

words.tr: adj. 整体论的；整体主义的；
words.ex: The doctor takes a holistic approach to health.
words.ex_cn: 这位医生采取整体论的方法来治疗健康问题。
words.en: A holistic approach to something involves considering the whole thing, rather than just a part of it.

words.tr:
n. 裂缝；叮铛声
v. 叮当响
words.ex: A small chink in the wall lets in light.
words.ex_cn: 墙上的一个小裂缝透进了光。
words.en: A chink is a narrow opening or crack, especially one that allows light through. It can also refer to a weak point in someone's character or in a system.

words.ex: The palace had opulent carpets and golden chandeliers.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿里有华丽的地毯和金色的吊灯。
words.en: Having or displaying great wealth or richness.

words.ex: The lake at dawn offers perfect tranquility.
words.ex_cn: 黎明时分的湖泊带来完全的宁静。
words.en: A state of peace and quiet.

words.ex: He added an annotation to the diagram.
words.ex_cn: 他在图表上添加了一个注释。
words.en: An annotation is a note or comment added to a text or diagram to explain or criticize it.

words.tr:
v. 防止；战斗；抑制；
n. 战斗；
words.ex: The new law aims to combat pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律旨在防止污染。
words.en: Combat refers to fighting, especially during a war. It can also mean to try to stop something harmful from happening or increasing.

words.tr: n. 有价值的人或物；长处；
words.ex: He is an asset to the team because he works hard.
words.ex_cn: 他是个有价值的人，因为他工作努力。
words.en: An asset is something valuable that an individual, corporation, or country owns or controls with the expectation that it will provide a future benefit.

words.ex: The wound caused a serious infection.
words.ex_cn: 伤口引起了严重的感染。
words.en: An infection is a disease caused by microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, or parasites invading the body.

words.ex: Farming is his main livelihood.
words.ex_cn: 务农是他的主要生计。
words.en: A person's livelihood is the way they earn money in order to live.

words.ex: The farmer feeds his livestock every morning.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天早上喂他的家畜。
words.en: Livestock are animals such as cattle and sheep which are kept on a farm.

words.ex: The movie was tame and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影枯燥无味。
words.en: If you describe an animal as tame, you mean that it is not afraid of humans and is not dangerous. If you describe a person or their behavior as tame, you mean that they are not very exciting or interesting.

words.tr:
v. 睡眠
n. 睡眠（常复数）
words.ex: The baby fell into a deep slumber after feeding.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝喂完奶后进入了深深的睡眠。
words.en: Slumber is a state of sleep, especially one that is peaceful and restful.

words.ex: The arboreal squirrel climbs high in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 这种树栖松鼠在高高的树上攀爬。
words.en: Relating to trees; living in trees.

words.tr:
n. 用力拉；拖拽；拖船
v. 用力拉；使劲拖；拖拽
words.ex: He gave a strong tug on the rope.
words.ex_cn: 他用力拉了绳子一下。
words.en: If you tug something or tug at it, you give it a quick and usually strong pull.

words.ex: He works in a custodial facility for juveniles.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个少年监禁设施工作。
words.en: Custodial is used to describe something relating to the legal responsibility for taking care of someone, especially a child, or for looking after property.

words.tr: adj. 不同的；多种多样的；
words.ex: The class has diverse students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级有来自许多国家的不同学生。
words.en: If a group or range of things is diverse, it is made up of a wide variety of things.

words.tr: v. 占主导地位；占支配地位；
words.ex: English predominate in this region.
words.ex_cn: 英语在这个地区占主导地位。
words.en: If one type of person or thing predominates in a group, there is more of that type than of any other.

words.ex: The fish swim among the coral in the sea.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在海中的珊瑚间游动。
words.en: A hard stony substance secreted by certain marine coelenterates as an external skeleton, typically forming large reefs in warm seas.

words.tr:
n. 纪律；学科；科目；训练；惩戒；
v. 约束自己；
words.ex: The teacher enforced discipline in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师在教室里维持纪律。
words.en: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

words.tr: adj. 天真无邪的；无辜的；
words.ex: The innocent child smiled at the stranger.
words.ex_cn: 那个天真无邪的孩子对陌生人笑了。
words.en: If someone is innocent, they did not commit a crime which they have been accused of.

words.ex: There is an inconsistency between his words and actions.
words.ex_cn: 他的言行不一致。
words.en: The quality or state of being inconsistent; lack of consistency.

words.ex: Overpopulation causes more traffic and pollution.
words.ex_cn: 人口过剩导致更多的交通和污染。
